STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r24.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r24.claim: During Moses' absence, the Israelites fashion a calf as an idol.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r24.anchor:
the Israelites fashioning a calf as an idol in his absence (vv.
148–54)

BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r1.claim: Moses returned from Mount Sinai intensely angry; the word asaf means anger, as in “when they angered Us.” God had informed him during the conversation that his people worshipped the calf.
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r1.anchor: حال كونه {غضبان أسفا} أي : شديد الغضب يقال آسفني فأسفت أي : أغضبني فغضبت

BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r2.claim: “You acted badly in my absence” condemns their conduct while Moses was away; mā is an indefinite descriptive noun explaining the implicit subject of biʾsa, with the condemned succession understood.
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r2.anchor: ساء ما عملتم خلفي أيها العبدة بعد غيبتي وانطلاقي إلى الجبل لأنه يقال خلفه بما يكره

BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r3.claim: The interrogative hamza rebukes them: they abandoned the Lord’s command before its proper completion, namely waiting faithfully for Moses and keeping his covenant.
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r3.anchor: الهمزة للإنكار أي أتركتموه غير تام كأنه ضمن عجل معنى سبق

BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r4.claim: Here the command can mean the commandments or what was commanded; haste is acting before its time and is blameworthy, unlike speed at the beginning of the proper time.
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r4.anchor: فالأمر واحد الأوامر أو أنه بمعنى المأمور به ، والعجلة : العمل بالشيء قبل وقته ولذلك صارت مذمومة بخلاف السرعة

BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r5.claim: The inward reading addresses the spirit’s qualities: they hastened back to worldly adornment and attachment before God’s command, interrupting the spiritual journey.
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r5.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : استعجلتم يا صفات الروح بالرجوع إلى الدنيا وزينتها والتعلق بها

BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r6.claim: Seekers and attendants of kings should turn from worldly things during the spiritual path; only after crossing the ego’s and desire’s wastes may they return to guide people to God.
BURSEVI:v3p185#2/r6.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن أرباب الطلب ، وأصحاب الملوك لا ينبغي أن يلتفتوا إلى شيء من الدنيا

BURSEVI:v3p185#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p185#3/r1.claim: Moses threw down the tablets of the Torah and pulled Aaron by the hair toward himself in reproach, not to humiliate him, supposing he had failed to restrain the people; Aaron was older, gentle, and loved by the Israelites.
BURSEVI:v3p185#3/r1.anchor: وألقى الالواح} التي كانت فيها التوراة من يده.

BURSEVI:v3p185#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p185#3/r2.claim: “Son of my mother” omits the vocative particle and its substitute alif for ease; although full brothers, Aaron names their mother to soften Moses and invite compassion, as Arabic custom does.
BURSEVI:v3p185#3/r2.anchor: {ابن أم} بحذف حرف النداء ، وأصله يا ابن أما حذفت الألف المبدلة من الياء

BURSEVI:v3p185#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p185#3/r3.claim: Aaron says the people overpowered him and nearly killed him to dispel Moses’s suspicion that he had been negligent: he had tried his utmost to stop them.
BURSEVI:v3p185#3/r3.anchor: إزاحة لتوهم التقصير في حقه ، والمعنى : بذلت وسعي في كفهم حتى قهروني واستضعفوني

BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r1.claim: Aaron asks Moses not to do anything that gives enemies cause to rejoice over him; the word denotes delight at an enemy’s misfortune, and such gloating is worse than any hardship.
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r1.anchor: {فلا تشمت بى الاعدآء} أي : فلا تفعل بي ما يكون سببا لشماتتهم بي

BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r2.claim: Aaron asks not to be counted among the wrongdoers through punishment or accusation of failure.
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r2.anchor: {ولا تجعلنى مع القوم الظالمين} أي : معدودا في عدادهم بالمؤاخذة

BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r3.claim: In the inward reading, Aaron is the heart, Moses the spirit, and their enemies the ego, Satan, and desire; the wrongdoers are heart’s qualities that worship the calf of the world.
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r3.anchor: أن هارون القلب أخ موسى الروح والأعداء النفس والشيطان والهوى والقوم الظالمون هم الذين عبدوا عجل الدنيا

BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r4.claim: The heart itself remains naturally oriented to loving and seeking God, though its qualities can take on the ego’s vices; the ego remains oriented to worldly desire while its qualities pass through spiritual states.
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r4.anchor: ولكن القلب من حيث هو هو لا يتغير عما جبل عليه من محبة الله وطلبه وإنما تتغير صفاته

BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r5.claim: If left to itself even briefly, the ego returns to its original nature; God’s established law does not change.
BURSEVI:v3p185#4/r5.anchor: ولو وكلت إلى نفسها طرفة عين لعادت المشومة إلى طبعها وجبلتها سنة الله التي قد خلت من قبل ولن تجد لسنة الله تبديلا

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r1.claim: Elmalılı says esef can mean either intense anger or grief, depending on whether the disliked event comes from an inferior or superior; for Moses it denotes anger toward his people and grief before God.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r1.anchor: hem de hüzün mânasına gelir. Ve yerine göre her birinde kullanılır.

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r2.claim: He defines esef as a state caused by something displeasing: when it comes from above it produces grief and constriction, and when from below it produces anger and agitation.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r2.anchor: o mekruh mâfevkten gelirse hüzün ve inkıbaz, mâdûndan gelirse gazab ve heyecan olur.

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r3.speaker: Ebu’d-Derdâ
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r3.claim: Abu al-Darda and many exegetes prefer the sense of intense anger, since the passage centers on Moses’ anger.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r3.anchor: evvelki Ebu’d-Derdâ radıyallâhu anh’ın kavli ve birçok müfessirînin muhtârıdır.

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r4.claim: Elmalılı favors the intense-anger reading in context, rendering the phrase as Moses returning angry and extremely angry.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r4.anchor: Yani غَضْبَٰنَ أَسِفًۭا kızarak ve son derece kızarak demektir.

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r5.claim: On his return from the meeting, Moses had learned from God that his people had adopted the calf, so he returned in intense anger.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r5.anchor: kavminin ıcl ittihaz ettiklerini min tarafillah haber almış ve bundan dolayı gazab ü şiddetle dönmüş

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r6.claim: Moses rebukes them for breaking his covenant and worshipping the calf after seeing his monotheistic worship and hearing his response to their earlier request for a god like others; their deputies also failed to stop the wrong.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r6.anchor: benim ahdime riayet etmeyerek arkamdan ne fena şeyler yaptınız ve buzağıya taptınız

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r7.claim: The rebuke also holds those left in charge responsible, since successors should honor their predecessor’s covenant and prevent such wrongdoing.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r7.anchor: makāmıma kāim olup böyle münkerâtı men‘etmesi lâzım gelenleriniz de bunu men‘etmediniz ha!

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r8.claim: One proposed reading of Moses’ question is that the people hurried to abandon their religion and God’s promises.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r8.anchor: Yani dinini ve vaadlerini acele edip bırakıverdiniz mi?

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r9.claim: Another proposed reading is that they impatiently expected the promised forty-night meeting to end, treating Moses as dead after thirty days and hastening to change their religion as other communities did after prophets.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r9.anchor: otuz gün geçer geçmez beni öldü farz ettiniz de peygamberlerinden bir zaman sonra birçok ümmetlerin dinlerini bozması âdet olduğu gibi siz de alelacele dininizi değiştirmeye mi kalktınız?

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r10.claim: A further interpretation is that they were rushing toward their Lord’s wrath and punishment.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r10.anchor: Veyahut alelacele Rabbinizin kahr u gazabını mı istediniz?

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r11.claim: A report says the tablets broke when Moses cast them down: six-sevenths were taken away and one remained, containing guidance and mercy while the removed portion contained detailed explanation of everything.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r11.anchor: Denilmiş ki bırakılınca elvâh kırılmış ve binâen‘aleyh yedide altısı ref‘olunmuş

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r12.claim: Elmalılı notes that the Qur’an contains no statement that the tablets broke in this way.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r12.anchor: lâkin Kur’an’da elvâhın böyle kırıldığını ifade eder bir kayıt görünmüyor

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r13.claim: He instead understands Moses to have temporarily set aside the tablets, which contained detailed guidance and mercy, so he could first address the crisis in the foundation of religion: monotheism.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r13.anchor: esas meseleyi şiddetle halletmek için tafsîlâta ait olan ve hüdâ ve rahmeti mutazammın bulunan elvâhı muvakkaten bir tarafa bırakmış

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r14.claim: The episode depicts something like declaring emergency rule in response to a grave upheaval threatening the foundation of monotheism.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r14.anchor: Bunda esâs-ı tevhîde ta‘alluk eden büyük bir ihtilâl karşısında idâre-i örfiye ilânına misâl veren bir hâdise tasvîri var demektir.

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r15.claim: By seizing Harun first, Moses shows that religious duty takes precedence even over regard for his brother.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r15.anchor: Din işinde evvelâ kardeş hatırına bile bakmıyor.

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r16.claim: Because Moses had appointed Harun as his successor, he begins by holding him responsible.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r16.anchor: Kardeşini yerine halef bırakmış olduğundan evvelemirde onun mes’ûliyetinden başlıyor.

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r17.claim: Moses’ first action also shows that working together with his brother for monotheism was the priority.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r17.anchor: Kardeş ile tevhîd-i mesâî etmek ilk iş olduğunu gösteriyor.

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r18.claim: Harun calls Moses “son of my mother” despite their being full brothers to awaken his tenderness: their mother signifies mercy, especially for Moses, and was a believer.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r18.anchor: Hazret-i Hârûn Hazret-i Mûsâ’nın şakīki, ana baba bir biraderi olduğu hâlde böyle hitap etmesi

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r19.claim: Harun says the people overpowered him and nearly killed him, then asks Moses not to give their enemies cause to gloat or count him among the unjust; he disowns their actions and says he did not deserve blame for failing to stop them.
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r19.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh düşmanları benimle şemâtet ettirme, yani bana düşmanları sevindirecek bir şey yapma.

ELMALILI:7:150-151/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:150-151/r20.claim: The cited poetic line says death is lighter than the enemies’ gloating, using shamatat for their malicious rejoicing.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r1.speaker: İbn İshak
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq's report says Moses did not know his people had worshipped the calf until he returned from Sinai.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r1.anchor: İbn İshak’tan nakledilen bir yoruma göre Hz. Mûsâ Tûr’dan dönünceye kadar kavminin buzağı heykeline taptığını bilmiyordu.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r2.speaker: İbn Cerîr et-Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r2.claim: Tabari says God informed Moses at Sinai that his people had fallen into this trial; 20:85 supports this view.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r2.anchor: İbn Cerîr et-Taberî’ye göre ise Mûsâ Tûr’da iken Allah onu, kavminin böyle bir fitneye bulaşmış olduğundan haberdar etmişti. Tâhâ sûresinin 85. âyeti de Taberî’nin bu görüşünü desteklemektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r3.claim: The Torah's account also agrees with Tabari's view.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r4.claim: Although Moses had repeatedly warned them against idolatry, the people abandoned monotheism during his short absence, deeply shocking him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r4.anchor: Mûsâ daha önce kavmini putperestlik konusunda sürekli uyardığı halde, kısa bir süre onlardan ayrılınca bütün bu uyarıları unutarak tevhid inancından sapmaları onu son derece sarsmıştı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r5.claim: Moses returned angry and rebuked the people; he also blamed Aaron, believing he had failed as deputy and failed to govern them properly.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r5.anchor: Zira kavmi putperestliğe sapmış, Hârûn da (Mûsâ’nın kanaatine göre) vekâlet görevini yerine getirmekte ve kavmini doğru dürüst yönetmekte kusur etmişti.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r6.claim: One explanation is that the people neglected or delayed God's ruling and, by rushing, altered and corrupted his law.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r6.anchor: Allah’ın hükmünü, yasasını uygulamakta veya beklemekte kusur ettiniz; acele davranarak O’nun yasasını değiştirip bozdunuz.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r7.claim: A second explanation is that they hurried toward incurring God's threat and wrath; 20:86 supports this reading.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r7.anchor: Allah’ın tehdidine ve gazabına uğramakta acele ettiniz.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r8.claim: Moses, deeply shaken, threw down the Torah tablets and seized Aaron by the head or hair, thinking he had allowed the calf worship; 20:92–93 says Moses blamed him for not coming to report it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r8.anchor: Hz. Mûsâ bu suretle kavmini suçlayarak, son derece sarsılmış bir hâletirûhiye içinde elindeki Tevrat levhalarını yere attı. Aynı duyguların tesiriyle

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r9.claim: Aaron appealed to Moses' compassion, saying he had tried to fulfill his duty and risked his life but could not control the Israelites.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r9.anchor: Hârûn da “Ey anam oğlu!…” diyerek merhamet duygusuna hitap ettiği Mûsâ’ya, görevini yapmaya çalıştığını, hatta bu uğurda hayatını bile tehlikeye soktuğunu, fakat İsrâiloğulları’na söz geçiremediğini ifade etti.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r10.claim: 20:94 reports Aaron considered further measures to stop calf worship but feared the matter would split the people and Moses would accuse him of causing division.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r10.anchor: Diğer bir âyette (Tâhâ 20/94) haber verildiğine göre Hârûn, kavmini altın buzağıya tapmaktan alıkoymak için başka önlemler almayı da düşünmüş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r11.claim: Aaron asked Moses not to make him ridiculous before the unjust calf-worshippers or treat him as one of them, since they were angry at Aaron's opposition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:150/r11.anchor: Hârûn, bütün bu açıklamalardan sonra Mûsâ’dan, hareketi ve sözleriyle kendisini hırpalayarak, yaptıklarına karşı çıktığı için ona kızgın olan “zalimler” (buzağı heykeline tapanlar) karşısında kendisini gülünç duruma düşürmemesini

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r1.claim: These readers read ابن أم with fatḥ on the mīm, as also in 20:94.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير، ونافع، وأبو عمرو، وحفص عن عاصم قال ابن أم نصبا، وفي طه [94] مثلها.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r2.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r2.claim: These readers break the mīm in ابن أم while keeping hamza rounded.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي: قال ابن أم بكسر الميم، فأما الهمزة فمضمومة

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r3.speaker: سيبويه
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r3.claim: Sibawayh says يا ابن أم and يا ابن عم are treated as one name because these forms are more common than يا ابن أبي or يا غلام غلامي.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r3.anchor: قالوا: يا ابن أم، ويا ابن عم؛ فجعلوا ذلك بمنزلة اسم واحد لأن هذا أكثر في كلامهم من يا ابن أبي

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r4.claim: The two words behave like one name but retain their underlying iḍāfa; Abu Zubayd’s يا ابن أمي shows the original form preserved.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r4.anchor: جعلوهما بمنزلة اسم واحد، ولم يرفضوا الأصل الذي هو إضافة الأول إلى الثاني

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r5.speaker: أبو زبيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r5.claim: Abu Zubayd’s poem uses يا ابن أمي and preserves the iḍāfa form, supporting Al-Farisi’s analysis.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r5.anchor:
ألا ترى قول أبي زبيد :
يا ابن أمي ويا شقيق نفسي ... أنت خليتني لأمر شديد

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r6.claim: In يا ابن أم, fatḥ on ابن is a built form based on its usual case-ending movement, not accusative case; compare لا رجل and the imperative مكانك.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r6.anchor: الفتحة في: ابن، ليست النصبة التي كانت تكون في الاسم المضاف المنادى

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r7.claim: Al-Farisi rejects deriving the fatḥ from an underlying يا ابن أما with deleted alif: a deleted vocative yāʾ is retained in a construct, and the cited يا بنت عما likewise keeps alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r7.anchor: قيل: ليس مثله، ألا ترى أن من حذف الياء من: يا غلام، أثبتها في يا غلام غلامي؟

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r8.claim: Final yāʾ can disappear at verse endings, as in 18:64 and 89:4, but that does not establish deletion of an underlying alif in يا ابن أم.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p89/r8.anchor: فحذف الياء من الفواصل، وما أشبه الفواصل من الكلام التام

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r5.claim: Mujāhid is reported with both تشمت and يشمت in the plea concerning the enemies.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r5.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة مجاهد: "فلا تشمت بي الأعداء"

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r6.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r6.claim: With الأعداء nominative, the enemies are the subject: the prayer asks God not to let them gloat over Moses, matching the common reading’s sense.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r6.anchor: قراءة مجاهد: "فلا تشمت بي الأعداء" رفع -كما ترى- بفعلهم، فالظاهر أن انصرافه إلى الأعداء

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r7.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r7.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r7.claim: With الأعداء accusative, the speaker directly tells God not to gloat over him, a construction comparable to attributing an action to God figuratively.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r7.anchor: فأما مع النصب فإنه كأنه قال: لا تشمت بي أنت يا رب، وجاز هذا كما قال سبحانه: {الله يستهزئ بهم}

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r8.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r8.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r8.claim: The accusative construction then returns to the intended sense by eliding a verb governing الأعداء, yielding the common reading’s meaning.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p259/r8.anchor: ثم عاد إلى المراد فأضمر فعلا نصب به الأعداء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p294/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p294/r4.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p294/r4.claim: They read ابن أم with fatḥa on mīm; Ibn Amir, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Asim in Abu Bakr's transmission use kasra, with hamza still ḍamma.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p294/r4.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم ﴿ قال ابن أم ﴾ نصبا وفى طه 94 مثله

QIRAAT-ER:7:150:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:150:13#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:150:13#1/r1.claim: The canonical variant opens the possessive yāʾ with fatḥa, a pronunciation change without semantic effect.
QIRAAT-ER:7:150:13#1/r1.anchor: open pronunciation of the first-person pronoun suffix, no semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:7:150:28#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:150:28#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:150:28#1/r1.claim: The kasra in ummi is the regular genitive of iḍāfa rather than vocative fatḥa, giving son of my mother.
QIRAAT-ER:7:150:28#1/r1.anchor: genitive by iḍāfa instead of vocative fatḥa

QIRAAT-ER:7:150:29#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:150:29#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:150:29#1/r1.claim: A second segment likewise identifies ummi with kasra as the standard genitive in iḍāfa.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p165#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p165#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p165#2/r9.claim: Asaf means grief; the verb is used as “he grieved.”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p165#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p165#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p165#2/r11.claim: Ishmāt means taking pleasure in the misfortune that befalls someone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p165#2/r11.anchor: الإشمات السرور بما ينال الشخص من المكروه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r6.claim: Moses returned from his communion with God to his people angry and sorrowful; when he confirmed their devotion to the calf, he cast down the tablets.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r6.anchor: ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال بئسما خلفتموني من بعدي أعجلتم أمر ربكم أي رجع من المناجاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r7.claim: A report says Moses heard the Israelites' sounds near their camp, called them idle people, then became angry and sorrowful when he found them worshiping the calf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r7.anchor: يروى أنه لما قرب من محلة بني إسرائيل سمع أصواتهم فقال هذه أصوات قوم لاهين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r8.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r8.claim: Al-Tabari says God informed Moses before he returned that his people had been seduced by the calf, explaining his anger; the author links this to the verse in Ta-Ha.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r8.anchor: وقال الطبري أخبره تعالى قبل رجوعه أنهم قد فتنوا بالعجل فلذلك رجع وهو غاضب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r9.claim: Ghaḍbān is an intensive form; anger is the heart boiling because something painful has happened.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r9.anchor: وغضبان من صفات المبالغة والغضب غليان القلب بسبب حصول ما يؤلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r10.claim: Accounts say Moses was among the quickest to anger and also quick to recover.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r10.anchor: وذكروا أنه عليه السلام كان من أسرع الناس غضبا وكان سريع الفيئة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r11.speaker: ابن القاسم عن مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r11.claim: Ibn al-Qasim says he heard Malik report that smoke rose from Moses' cap and his body hair stood over his garment when he was angry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن القاسم: سمعت مالكا يقول كان إذا غضب طلع الدخان من قلنسوته ورفع شعر بدنه جبته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and al-Suddi interpret asaf as sorrowful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r12.anchor: قاله ابن عباس والحسن والسدي أو الجزع قاله مجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r13.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r13.claim: Mujahid interprets asaf as distress or agitation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r14.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r14.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and Ibn Atiyya say asaf can mean grieving or intensely angry, and it most often means sorrowful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r14.anchor: أو المتلهف أو الشديد الغضب قاله الزمخشري وابن عطية قال: وأكثر ما يكون بمعنى الحزين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r15.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r15.claim: Ibn Qutayba gives angered and regretful as additional meanings of asaf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r15.anchor: أو المغضب قاله ابن قتيبة أو النادم قاله القتبي أيضا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r16.speaker: الواحدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r16.claim: Al-Wahidi says the meanings of asaf are close: what comes from someone below angers, while what comes from someone above causes grief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r16.anchor: أو متقاربان قاله الواحدي قال: فإذا أتاك ما تكره ممن دونك غضبت أو ممن فوقك حزنت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r17.claim: The calf worship angered Moses, while God's having tested his people grieved him, as God had already told him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r17.anchor: فأغضبه عبادتهم العجل وأحزنه فتنة الله إياهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r18.claim: The rebuke 'you took my place badly' may address the Samaritan and calf worshipers for substituting the calf for worship of God, or Israel's leaders, including Aaron and believers, for failing to stop the idolatry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r18.anchor: والخطاب إما للسامري وعباد العجل أي بئسما قمتم مقامي حيث عبدتم العجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r19.claim: The phrase 'after me' means after Israel had witnessed Moses' monotheism, or after he had taught them monotheism and restrained their desires to worship cattle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r19.anchor: وخلفتموني يدل على البعدية في الزمان والمعنى هنا من بعد ما رأيتم مني توحيد الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r20.claim: A successor is expected to follow the predecessor's way; khalafahu bi-khayr or bi-sharr means he did good or evil after the predecessor left.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p179#2/r20.anchor: ومن حق الخلف أن يسير سيرة المستخلف ولا يخالفه ويقال خلفه بخير أو شر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains ʿajila ʿan as leaving an affair unfinished; the causative form means making someone hurry away and implies outstripping the appointed time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r2.anchor: يقال: عجل عن الأمر إذا تركه غير تام ونقيضه تم عليه وأعجله عنه غيره ويضمن معنى سبق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads Moses as accusing them of abandoning the wait for God's command and covenant, assuming his appointed time had ended and he had died, then changing religion like earlier nations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r3.anchor: والمعنى أعجلتم عن أمر ربكم وهو انتظار موسى حافظين لعهده وما وصاكم به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reports that the Samaritan told them the calf was their and Moses' god and Moses would not return because he had died.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r4.anchor: وروي أن السامري قال لهم أحين أخرج إليهم العجل هذا إلهكم وإله موسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya interprets the question as asking whether they tried to outpace God's decree and hastened Moses' arrival before the appointed time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: معناه أسابقتم قضاء ربكم واستعجلتم إتياني من قبل الوقت الذي قدرته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r6.speaker: يعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r6.claim: Yaʿqub distinguishes ʿajiltu al-shayʾ, being ahead of a thing, from aʿjaltu al-rajul, making a person hurry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r6.anchor: وقال يعقوب: يقال عجلت الشيء سبقته وأعجلت الرجل استعجلته أي حملته على العجلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r7.claim: Other interpretations take the question to mean that they hastened God's forty-night appointment, His wrath, or their worship of the calf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه أعجلتم ميعاد ربكم أربعين ليلة، وقيل: أعجلتم سخط ربكم، وقيل: أعجلتم بعبادة العجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r8.claim: Haste means advancing something before its proper time and is blameworthy, unlike the praised promptness in Moses' words 'I hastened to You, Lord, to please You.'
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r8.anchor: وقيل: العجلة التقدم بالشيء في غير وقته، قيل: وهي مذمومة ويضعفه قوله وعجلت إليك رب لترضى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r9.claim: The tablets were the Torah; Moses, carrying them, set them down in anger at the calf worship and zeal for God's religion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r9.anchor: وألقى الألواح وأخذ برأس أخيه يجره إليه أي الألواح التوراة وكان حاملا لها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r10.claim: The Israelites reportedly loved Aaron more than Moses because Aaron had a gentler disposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r10.anchor: وقالوا كان هارون ألين منه خلقا ولذلك كان أحب إلى بني إسرائيل منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r11.claim: Another view says Moses dropped the tablets in shock at what had happened to his people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r11.anchor: وقيل: ألقاها دهشا لما دهمه من أمرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says the tablets broke when Moses dropped them; he recovered the greater part containing detailed knowledge, while the remaining piece held guidance and mercy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r12.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: أن موسى عليه السلام لما ألقاها تكسرت فرفع أكثرها الذي فيه تفصيل كل شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r13.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r13.claim: A group of exegetes say six sevenths of the tablets were taken up and one seventh remained.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r13.anchor: وروي أنها رفع ستة أسباعها وبقي سبع قاله جماعة من المفسرين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r14.speaker: أبو الفرج بن الجوزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r14.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi says it is unsound that Moses threw the tablets in a way that broke them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r14.anchor: وقال أبو الفرج بن الجوزي لا يصح أنه رماها رمي كاسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r15.claim: The author says Moses merely set the tablets down: his hands had to be free to seize Aaron, and the later statement that he took them again shows they neither broke nor lost portions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r15.anchor: والظاهر أنه ألقاها من يديه لأنهما كانتا مشغولتين بها وأراد إمساك أخيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r16.claim: The apparent meaning of taking Aaron by the head is that Moses actually grasped and pulled his head toward him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r16.anchor: والظاهر أنه أخذ برأسه أي أمسك رأسه جاره إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r17.claim: Other views say Moses took Aaron by his hair, locks and beard, beard alone, or ear, or only gestured rather than physically seizing him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r17.anchor: وقيل: بشعر رأسه، وقيل: بذوائبه ولحيته، وقيل: بلحيته، وقيل: بأذنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r18.claim: The author supports this explanation by pointing to the later account of Moses anger subsiding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r18.anchor: ويدل على هذا الظاهر قوله: ولما سكت عن موسى الغضب وقوله:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r19.claim: The apparent explanation is that Moses seized Aaron in anger at his failure to prevent calf worship despite being appointed over the Israelites and commanded to reform them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p181/r19.anchor: والظهر أن سبب هذا الأخذ هو غضبه على أخيه وكيف عبدوا العجل وهو قد استخلفه فيهم وأمره بالإصلاح وأن لا يتبع سبيل من أفسد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r1.speaker: هارون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r1.claim: Aaron's appeal that Moses not seize him by beard or head, and his fear of dividing Israel, is quoted from Ta-Ha.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r1.anchor: إني خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says Moses dragged Aaron by the hair and locks in the shock of the event, suspecting Aaron had failed to restrain the people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أي بشعر رأسه يجره إليه بذوائبه وذلك لشدة ما ورد عليه من الأمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r3.claim: One view says Moses grabbed Aaron only to tell him privately that the tablets had descended during his communion, and Aaron stopped him lest the Israelites mistake the private exchange for humiliation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r3.anchor: وقيل: ذلك الأخذ والجر كان ليسر إليه أنه نزل عليه الألواح في مناجاته وأراد أن يخفيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r4.claim: Another view says Moses pulled Aaron close to learn what happened; Aaron feared the Israelites would think Moses was humiliating him and explained their oppression.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r4.anchor: وقيل: ضمه ليعلم ما لديه فكره ذلك هارون لئلا يظنوا إهانته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r5.claim: Another view treats the gesture as affection rather than insult, like Arabs seizing a brother's beard.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r5.anchor: وقيل: كان ذلك على سبيل الإكرام لا على سبيل الإهانة كما تفعل العرب من قبض الرجل على لحية أخيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r6.claim: Aaron addresses Moses as 'son of my mother' to plead weakness and tenderness; Arabs commonly invoke the mother to soften a brother, as in cited poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r6.anchor: ناداه نداء استضعاف وترفق وكان شقيقه وهي عادة العرب تتلطف وتتحنن بذكر الأم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r7.claim: The source says their mother was a believer, while their father was cut off from kin by disbelief, as in God's statement to Noah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r7.anchor: وأيضا فكانت أمهما مؤمنة قالوا: وكان أبوه مقطوعا عن القرابة بالكفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r8.claim: Aaron invoked their mother because her right was greater through the hardship of bearing, raising, and caring for him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r8.anchor: وأيضا لما كان حقها أعظم لمقاساتها الشدائد في حمله وتربيته والشفقة عليه ذكره بحقها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r9.speaker: الحرميان وأبو عمرو وحفص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r9.claim: The two Medinan readers, Abu Amr, and Hafs read ibn umma with a fatḥa on mīm; the Kufans analyze it as the shortened form of yā ibn ummāh and an inflected possessive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان وأبو عمرو وحفص: ابن أم بفتح الميم، فقال الكوفيون: أصله يا ابن أماه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r10.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r10.claim: Sibawayh analyzes ibn umma with an open mīm as two nouns compounded and built on fatḥa, rather than a genitive possessive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r10.anchor: وقال سيبويه: هما اسمان بنيا على الفتح كاسم واحد كخمسة عشر ونحوه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r11.speaker: باقي السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r11.claim: The remaining canonical readers use a kasra on mīm; the Kufan analysis treats the form as inflected with the possessive yāʾ omitted and represented by kasra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r11.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة بكسر الميم فقياس قول الكوفيين أنه معرب وحذفت ياء المتكلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r12.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r12.claim: For the kasra form, Sibawayh says it is built and attached to the possessive yāʾ, omitted with its kasra retained; an ordinary construct-state form could not drop the yāʾ because it is not itself vocative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r12.anchor: وقال سيبويه هو مبني أضيف إلى ياء المتكلم كما قالوا يا أحد عشر أقبلوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p182/r13.claim: A recitation also retains the possessive yāʾ explicitly.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r1.claim: Among the forms, the best is omitting the possessive yāʾ with its kasra retained; other possible forms change it to alif and vary the tāʾ and mīm vowels, including in related kinship calls.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r1.anchor: وأجود اللغات الاجتزاء بالكسرة عن ياء الإضافة ثم قلب الياء ألفا والكسرة قبلها فتحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r2.claim: Other attested forms include yā ibn ummi with the yāʾ retained and ibn imi with kasra on hamza and mīm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r2.anchor: وقرىء يا ابن أمي بإثبات الياء وابن إم بكسر الهمزة والميم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r3.claim: The vocative and the following sentence together complete what was said, to soften Moses' anger and excuse Aaron as having warned them as far as his strength allowed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r3.anchor: ومعمول القول المنادى والجملة بعده المقصود بها تخفيف ما أدرك موسى من الغضب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r4.claim: Aaron's explanation shows he had not failed to admonish and warn; the people overpowered him and ignored his counsel, nearly killing him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r4.anchor: ولكنهم استضعفوه فلم يلتفتوا إلى وعظه بل قاربوا أن يقتلوه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r5.claim: Istadaʿafūnī means they found or considered me weak, derived from the sense of finding something to be as its verbal root expresses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r5.anchor: ومعنى استضعفوني وجدوني فهي بمعنى إلفاء الشيء بمعنى ما صيغ منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r6.claim: After explaining the people's oppression and near attempt to kill him, Aaron asks Moses not to make the enemies rejoice by harming him, which would make him blameworthy before both them and Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r6.anchor: ولما أبدى له ما كان منهم من الاستضعاف له ومقاربة قتلهم إياه سأله ترك ما يسرهم بفعله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r7.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r7.claim: A poet says death is preferable to the enemies' gloating.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r8.speaker: ابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r8.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads tashmat with fatḥa on tāʾ, kasra on mīm, and the enemies in the accusative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن تشمت بفتح التاء وكسر الميم ونصب الأعداء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r9.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r9.claim: Mujahid reads tashmat with both tāʾ and mīm open and the enemies in the accusative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r9.anchor: ومجاهد كذلك إلا أنه فتح الميم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r10.speaker: أبو الفتح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r10.claim: Abu al-Fath construes Mujahid's reading intransitively as a prayer that God not gloat, supplying an omitted verb for 'the enemies'; the author calls this strained because shamit is attested as transitive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r10.anchor: وخرج أبو الفتح قراءة مجاهد على أن تكون لازمة والمعنى فلا تشمت أنت يا رب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r11.claim: The author rejects Abu al-Fath's strained intransitive reading: shamit is reported as transitive, so no omitted verb is needed; the comparisons with God's mockery or plotting are replies to opponents, not initiated speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r11.anchor: وهذا خروج عن الظاهر وتكلف في الإعراب وقد روي تعدي شمت لغة فلا يتكلف أنها لازمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r12.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r12.claim: Mujahid also has tashmat with both vowels open and al-aʿdāʾ nominative, while Humayd ibn Qays has a kasra on mīm; they make the verb intransitive with enemies as its subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r12.anchor: وعن مجاهد فلا تشمت بفتح التاء والميم ورفع الأعداء، وعن حميد بن قيس كذلك إلا أنه كسر الميم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r13.claim: On the intransitive readings, the surface wording tells the enemies not to gloat, while the intended plea to Aaron is not to expose Moses to harm that would make them rejoice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r13.anchor: فظاهره أنه نهى الأعداء عن الشماتة به وهو من باب لا أرينك هنا والمراد نهيه أخاه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r14.claim: Aaron first asks that Moses not give the enemies a visible cause for gloating, then asks not to be judged or treated as one of the wrongdoers, a less visible inner judgment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r14.anchor: وبدأ أولا بسؤال أخيه أن لا يشمت به الأعداء لأن ما يوجب الشماتة هو فعل مكروه ظاهر لهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r15.claim: The final plea can mean that Moses should not make Aaron a companion of the wrongdoers in his anger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p183/r15.anchor: أو يكون المعنى ولا تجعلني في موجدتك علي قرينا لهم مصاحبا لهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r1.claim: Once the people recognized the ugliness of their deed, they drank the cup of regret and feared loss unless God's gentle favor rescued them.
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r1.anchor: حين تحققوا بقبح صنيعهم تجرعوا كاسات الأسف ندما

QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r2.claim: Even a harmonious reunion with his people would have been troubled for Moses by losing intimate speech with God and returning to witness created beings.
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r2.anchor: لكان متنغص العيش لما مني به من حرمان سماع الخطاب والرد إلى شهود الأغيار

QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r3.claim: Moses faced several possible ordeals: loss of divine speech, being kept from asking to see God, and witnessing Israel's temptation and desire for the calf.
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r3.anchor: ولا يدرى أي المحن كانت أشد على موسى

QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r4.claim: Hearing that his people were tested affected Moses less than seeing their condition with his own eyes.
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r4.anchor: لما شاهدهم أثرت فيه المشاهدة بما لم يؤثر فيه السماع

QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r5.claim: Harun says “son of my mother” to soften Moses and appeal for mercy.

QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r6.claim: Harun's plea about his beard and head says he has endured repeated ordeals and asks Moses not to add to his suffering but to console him.

QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r7.claim: Harun's appeal softened Moses, who returned to God in supplication and confessed his need for forgiveness and mercy.

QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r10.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r10.claim: An unnamed interpretation assigns the sin to the Israelites and the apologetic to Moses and Harun, as an expression of pure servitude.
QUSHAYRI:v1p358/r10.anchor: ارتكاب الذنب كان من بني إسرائيل

ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء ومحمد القرظي وعطاء والزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r1.claim: They take أسفا to mean intense anger, while other authorities take it to mean sorrow.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r1.anchor: كما قال أبو الدرداء و محمد القرظي وعطاء والزجاج أو حزينا على ما روي عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Qatada are reported to understand أسفا as sorrow.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r2.anchor: أو حزينا على ما روي عن ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة رضي الله تعالى عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r3.claim: Abu Muslim says anger and sorrow have the same meaning here, so the wording repeats itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم : الغضب والأسف بمعنى والتكرير

ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r4.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi says the terms are close: displeasure from someone beneath you produces anger, while displeasure from someone above you produces sorrow; Moses was angry at the calf worship and sorrowful that God tested his people after warning him.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r4.anchor: وقال الواحدي : هما متقاربان فإذا جاءك ما تكره ممن هو دونك غضبت وإذا جاءك ممن هو فوقك حزنت

ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r5.claim: The two descriptions are either parallel circumstantial clauses or nested, with the second describing the hidden pronoun in the first; Abu al-Baqa also allows the second to replace the first as a full substitute.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r5.anchor: ونصب الوصفين على أنهما حالان مترادفان أو متداخلان بأن يكون الثاني حالا من الضمير المستتر في الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r6.claim: Moses' rebuke may address the calf worshippers, or Aaron and the believers with him: in the first case he blames their worship after his teaching of monotheism; in the second, their failure to keep his trust and restrain the worshippers.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r6.anchor: خطاب إما لعبدة العجل وإما لهارون عليه السلام ومن معه من المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r7.claim: The address may include both groups, with succession referring to both forms of Moses' entrusted work; من بعدي does not repeat خلفتموني because it can mean after his period of authority, or emphasize the deputy's portrayal of Moses' way.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r7.anchor: وجوز أن يكون على الخطاب للفريقين على أن المراد بالخلافة الخلافة فيما يعم الأمرين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r8.claim: ما is an indefinite descriptive noun qualifying the hidden subject of بئس; the omitted object of blame is their bad succession of Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r8.anchor: و ( ما ) نكرة موصوفة مفسرة لفاعل بئس المستكن فيه والمخصوص بالذم محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r9.claim: If Moses addresses Aaron and the faithful, he condemns their failure to fulfill the succession rather than the office itself; for the Samiri's followers, the blame is straightforward.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r9.anchor: والذم فيما إذا كان الخطاب لهارون عليه السلام ومن معه من المؤمنين ليس للخلافة نفسها بل لعدم الجري على مقتضاها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r10.claim: أعجلتم أمر ربكم means they rushed ahead of God's command to wait for Moses and preserve his covenant, assuming the appointed time had ended and he would not return.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r10.anchor: أي أعجلتم عما أمركم به ربكم وهو إنتظار موسى عليه السلام حال كونهم حافظين لعهده وما وصاهم به

ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r11.claim: A report says al-Samiri told them the calf was their god and Moses would not return because he had died; another says they counted twenty days and nights as forty before making the calf.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r11.anchor: روي أن السامري قال لهم حين أخرج لهم العجل وقال : إن هذا إلهكم وإله موسى إن موسى لن يرجع وإنه قد مات

ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r12.claim: Although عجل normally takes عن with أمر to mean leaving something unfinished, the verb here includes the sense of السبق, preemption, and so takes that construction; Yaqub instead treats preemption as its literal meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r12.anchor: وذهب يعقوب إلى أن السبق معنى حقيقي له من غير تضمين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r13.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r13.claim: Al-Hasan understands the phrase as hastening God's promise of forty days, taking أمر to mean a promise or affair rather than a command; al-Tibi says these forty are distinct from the forty nights in 7:142.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p65#2/r13.anchor: وعن الحسن أن المعنى أعجلتم وعد ربكم الذي وعدكم من الأربعين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r1.claim: Moses set the tablets down in haste to free his hand to seize Aaron, driven by intense religious zeal against the people's idolatry; calling it a throwing heightens blame on the people and signals his fervor without disrespecting scripture.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r1.anchor: فعجل في وضع الألواح لتفرغ يده فيأخذ برأس أخيه فعبر عن ذلك الوضع بالإلقاء تفظيعا لفعل قومه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r2.claim: A report says that when Moses became angry, his cap would blaze like fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r2.anchor: أخرج أبو الشيخ عن زيد بن أسلم أنه عليه السلام كان إذا غضب إشتعلت قلنسوته نارا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r3.speaker: القاضي ناصر الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r3.claim: Al-Qadi explains the throwing as an act of severe anger and religious indignation, and reports that some tablets broke when Moses cast them down.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r3.anchor: وقال القاضي ناصر الدين : أي طرحها من شدة الغضب وفرط الضجرة حمية للدين ثم نقل أنه انكسر بعضها حين ألقاها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r4.speaker: صبغة الله أفندي الحيدري
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r4.claim: Haydari objects that zeal for religion should have made Moses protect God's book from loss or dishonor, including broken tablets.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r4.anchor: بأن الحمية للدين إنما تقتضي إحترام كتاب الله تعالى وحمايته أن يلحق به نقص أو هوان

ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r5.speaker: صبغة الله أفندي الحيدري
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r5.claim: Haydari's alternative is that Moses lost self-control and the tablets fell involuntarily; describing this as throwing treats failure to restrain himself as intentional, since the righteous are judged by the standard of the spiritually near.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r5.anchor: والصواب أن يقال : إنه عليه السلام لفرط حميته الدينية وشدة غضبه لله تعالى لم يتمالك ولم يتماسك إن وقعت الألواح من يده بدون إختيار

ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r6.speaker: صالح أفندي الموصلي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r6.claim: Al-Mawsili says Haydari misread al-Qadi: religious zeal was not the stated cause of throwing; anger and agitation are the two competing causal complements, and al-Qadi's interpretation permits the verse's wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r6.anchor: بأنه لايخفى أن هذا الإيراد إنما نشأ من جعل قول القاضي حمية للدين مفعولا له لطرحها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r7.claim: Alusi finds al-Mawsili's claim about al-Qadi's intent unclear and rejects treating the verse as a rebuke of Moses, since neither its lead-in nor context supports that reading; the passage censures his people.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r7.anchor: ليس في السباق ولا في السياق ما يقضي بكون المقام عتاب موسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r8.claim: The tablets' breakage was neither intended nor anticipated; the authorized setting-down arose from haste and zeal for God, comparable to Moses hastening to please his Lord.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r8.anchor: وإنكسار بعض الألواح حصل من فعل مأذون فيه ولم يكن غرض موسى عليه السلام ولا مر بباله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r9.claim: Reports disagree about how many tablets broke and were restored, while some deny any breakage because the Qur'an's apparent wording points otherwise.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r9.anchor: واختلفت الروايات في مقدار ما تكسر ورفع وبعضهم أنكر ذلك حيث أن ظاهر القرآن خلافه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reports from the Prophet that God had told Moses his people were tested, but Moses did not cast the tablets until he saw them; some then broke.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يرحم الله تعالى موسى ليس المعاين كالمخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r11.claim: A report says six sevenths of the tablets were lifted and one seventh remained, with a similar report from others.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r11.anchor: وما روي عن ابن عباس أن موسى عليه السلام لما ألقى الإلواح رفع منها ستة أسباع وبقي سبع وكذا ما روي عن غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r12.claim: Alusi says the six-sevenths report conflicts with reports that the Torah came in seventy portions, was read in a year, and was fully read by only Moses, Joshua, Ezra, and Jesus; it also conflicts with the later mention of taking the tablets.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p66/r12.anchor: مناف لما روي فيما تقدم من أن التوراة نزلت سبعين وقرأ يقرأ الجزء منه في سنة لم يقرأها إلا أربعة نفر موسى ويوشع وعزير وعيسى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r1.claim: Taking Aaron by the head means grasping his hair, the customary way to hold a head; this can coexist with the Ta-Ha account of taking his beard, either by inclusion or by extending the grasp.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r1.anchor: أي بشعر رأس هارون عليه السلام لأنه الذي يؤخذ ويمسك عادة ولا ينافي أخذه بلحيته كما وقع في سورة طه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r2.claim: Moses thought Aaron had failed to restrain the people and, in overwhelming anger, seized him; Aaron was three years older, while Moses held the higher rank and independent leadership and Aaron served as his minister.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r2.anchor: ظنا منه عليه السلام أنه قصر في كفهم ولم يتمالك لشدة غضبه وفرط غيضه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r3.claim: Moses did not intend to humiliate Aaron; the physical reproach addressed what seemed a failure of duty under his leadership, born of religious zeal.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r3.anchor: ولم يقصد موسى بهذا الأخذ إهانته والإستخفاف به بل اللوم الفعلي على التقصير المظنون بحكم الرياسة وفرط الحمية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r4.claim: Alusi rejects the suggestions that Moses grabbed Aaron to whisper and learn the details, or to calm him because he appeared distressed.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r4.anchor: والقول بأنه عليه السلام إنما أخذ رأس أخيه ليساره ويستكشف منه كيفية الواقعة مما يأباه الذوق

ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r5.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r5.claim: Al-Jubba'i says Moses treated Aaron as himself, doing to him what a person does in intense anger.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r5.anchor: وقال أبو علي الجبائي : إن موسى عليه السلام أجرى أخاه مجرى نفسه فصنع به ما يصنع الإنسان به عند شدة الغضب

ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r6.speaker: الشيخ المفيد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r6.claim: The Shi'i al-Mufid says Moses seized Aaron to show the people, in the strongest way, how grave their error was and deter them; Alusi finds this less likely.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r6.anchor: وقال الشيخ المفيد من الشيعة : إن ذلك للتألم من ضلال قومه وإعلامهم على أبلغ وجه عظم ما فعلوه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r7.claim: Alusi prefers his earlier explanation of Moses' anger and haste over al-Mufid's account, which would make Moses punish Aaron for the people's offense.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r7.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الأمر على هذا من قبيل : غيري جنى وأنا المعاقب فيكم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r8.claim: The clause يجره إليه is circumstantial and may modify Moses' pronoun, the head, or Aaron; Abu al-Baqa considers these attachments weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r8.anchor: وجملة ( يجره ) في موضع الحال من ضمير موسى أو من رأس أو من أخيه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r9.claim: Aaron's ابن أم omits the vocative particle because the moment is urgent; calling him son of their mother softens the appeal, though they were full brothers according to the strongest view.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r9.anchor: ابن أم ( بحذف حرف النداء لضيق المقام وتخصيص الأم بالمذكر مع كونهما شقيقين على الأصح للترقيق

ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r10.claim: Other explanations for mentioning their mother are that she raised Moses through dangers, or that Aaron's visible mercy made the maternal reference fitting; the latter draws on his prophetic gift and merciful speech to the people.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r10.anchor: وقيل : لأنها قامت بتربيته وقاست في تخليصه المخاوف والشدائد وقيل : إن هارون عليه السلام كانت آثار الجمال والرحمة فيه ظاهرة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r11.claim: The maternal appeal has a Sufi rationale: mercy is most complete in the mother, who raises and bears hardships for her child.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r11.anchor: ومن هنا ذكر الأم ونسب إليها لأن الرحمة فيها أتم ولولاها ما قدرت على تربية الولد وتحمل المشاق فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r12.claim: Several names are proposed for Moses and Aaron's mother; some claim her name has occult power to unlock locks through ritual practices, which Alusi dismisses as invented asceticism without divine warrant.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p67/r12.anchor: واختلف في إسم أمهما عليهما السلام فقيل : محيانة بنت يصهر بن لاوي وقيل : يوحانذ وقيل : يارخا وقيل : يازخت

ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r1.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r1.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr from Asim read ابن أم with a genitive ending, from ابن أمي with the ya deleted and its kasra retained for ease; the other readers use fatḥ for further ease or by analogy with a compound numeral.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسلئي وأبوبكر عن عاصم هنا وفي طه ( ابن أم ) بالكسر وأصله ابن أمي فحذفت الياء

ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r2.claim: Aaron says the people overpowered and humiliated him and disregarded him because he had few supporters.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r2.anchor: ( استضعفوني ( أي إستذلوني وقهروني ولم يبالوا بي لقلة أنصاري

ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r3.claim: Aaron says they nearly killed him when he forbade their conduct, and means that he had exerted every effort to stop them.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r3.anchor: وقاربوا قتلي حين نهيتهم عن ذلك والمراد أني بذلت وسعي في كفهم ولم آل جهدا في منعهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r4.claim: Aaron asks Moses not to give the enemies cause to rejoice over him; schadenfreude is an enemy's pleasure at another's misfortune, and they do not understand Moses' motive.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r4.anchor: أي فلا تفعل مايشمتون بي لأجله فإنهم لايعلمون سر فعلك والشماتة سرور العدو بما يصيب المرء من مكروه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r5.claim: A variant reading makes the verb intransitive, so the enemies themselves rejoice over Aaron; the phrase still conveys the same meaning, and the explicit noun replaces their pronoun rhetorically.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r5.anchor: وقريء ( فلا تشمت بي الأعداء ) بفتح حرف المضارعة وضم الميم ورفع الأعداء

ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r6.claim: Aaron asks not to be counted among the wrongdoers, not to be treated like them in the rebuke, or not to be considered one of them when innocent of their deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r6.anchor: أي لاتجعلني معدودا في عدادهم ولا تسلك بي سلوكك بهم في المعاتبة أو لا تعتقدني واحدا من الظالمين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r7.claim: The construction of جعل here resembles the Qur'anic usage in which people made the angels female.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p68/r7.anchor: فالجعل مثله في قوله تعالى : ( وجعلوا الملائكة الذين هم عباد الرحمن إناثا )

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r1.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ says أسفا means intense anger; Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Suddī say it means grief, the most intense grief.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r1.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء: الأسف شديد الغضب. وقال ابن عباس والسدي: أسفا أي حزينا. والأسف أشد الحزن،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r2.claim: Moses’s ‘evil are your successors’ means they acted badly after his departure; خلفه بخير or بشر means to leave one’s household well or badly while away.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r2.anchor: أي: بئس ما عملتهم بعد ذهابي، يقال: خلفه بخير أو بشر إذا أولاه في أهله بعد شخوصه عنهم خيرا أو شرا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r3.claim: أعجلتم means ‘did you outpace’; al-Ḥasan says it refers to God’s promise of forty nights, while al-Kalbī says they hastened to worship the calf before God’s command came.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r3.anchor: {أعجلتم} أسبقتم {أمر ربكم} قال الحسن: وعد ربكم الذي وعدكم من الأربعين 138/أليلة. وقال الكلبي: أعجلتم بعبادة العجل قبل أن يأتيكم أمر ربكم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r4.claim: Moses threw the tablets bearing the Torah to the ground in the intensity of his anger.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r4.anchor: {وألقى الألواح} التي فيها التوراة وكان حاملا لها، فألقاها على الأرض من شدة الغضب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r5.speaker: الرواة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r5.claim: The narrators say the Torah consisted of seven portions; the tablets broke, six portions containing unseen reports were lifted, and one remained with admonition, rulings, lawful and forbidden matters.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r5.anchor: قالت الرواة: كانت التوراة سبعة أسباع، فلما ألقى الألواح تكسرت فرفعت ستة أسباعها وبقي سبع،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r6.claim: Moses seized Aaron by his forelocks and beard; Aaron was three years older and more beloved to Israel because he was less quick to anger.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r6.anchor: {وأخذ برأس أخيه} بذوائبه ولحيته {يجره إليه} وكان هارون أكبر من موسى بثلاث سنين وأحب إلى بني إسرائيل من موسى، لأنه كان لين الغضب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r7.claim: Kufa and Syrian readers break the mīm in ابن أم, omitting the possessive yāʾ while its kasra signals ‘my mother’; Ḥijāz, Basra, and Ḥafṣ open it, meaning ‘son of my mother.’
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r7.anchor: {ابن أم} قرأ أهل الكوفة والشام هاهنا وفي طه بكسر الميم، يريد يا ابن أمي، فحذف ياء الإضافة وأبقيت الكسرة لتدل على الإضافة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r8.claim: Another grammatical explanation treats ابن أم as one compound noun built on fatḥa, like Ḥaḍramawt and fifteen; Moses used the phrase to soften Aaron and elicit sympathy, though another view says they shared only a mother.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r8.anchor: وقيل: جعله اسما واحدا وبناه على الفتح، كقولهم: حضرموت، وخمسة عشر، ونحوهما، وإنما قال ابن أم وكان هارون أخاه لأبيه وأمه ليرققه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r9.claim: ‘The people weakened me’ means the calf worshippers overpowered Aaron and nearly killed him; he asks Moses not to let the enemies rejoice or count him among the wrongdoers, meaning calf worshippers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p284/r9.anchor: {إن القوم استضعفوني} يعني عبدة العجل، {وكادوا يقتلونني} هموا وقاربوا أن يقتلوني، {فلا تشمت بي الأعداء ولا تجعلني}

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r1.claim: Asifan means intensely angry, or it may mean sorrowful.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r2.claim: Moses condemns the people for worshiping the calf; alternatively, the address is to Aaron and the believers for taking his place without restraining the worshipers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r2.anchor: فعلتم بعدي حيث عبدتم العجل، والخطاب للعبدة أو أقمتم مقامي فلم تكفوا العبدة والخطاب لهارون والمؤمنين معه!

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r3.claim: The indefinite mā is descriptive and explains the concealed subject of biʾsa; the omitted object of blame is their bad succession in his place.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r3.anchor: وما نكرة موصوفة تفسر المستكن في بئس والمخصوص بالذم محذوف تقديره بئس خلافة خلفتمونيها من بعدي خلافتكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r4.claim: “After me” means after Moses departed, or after they witnessed his teaching of monotheism, transcendence, and restraint from what contradicts it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r4.anchor: من بعد انطلاقي، أو من بعد ما رأيتم مني من التوحيد والتنزيه والحمل عليه والكف عما ينافيه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r5.claim: “Were you impatient with your Lord's command?” means leaving it unfinished, with ʿajila carrying the sense of sabaqa, or impatiently changing the promised forty-day return as nations altered things after their prophets.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r5.anchor: أتركتموه غير تام، كأنه ضمن عجل معنى سبق فعدى تعديته، أو أعجلتم وعد ربكم الذي وعدنيه من الأربعين وقدرتم موتي وغيرتم بعدي كما غيرت الأمم بعد أنبيائهم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r6.claim: He cast down the tablets from intense anger and religious zeal.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r6.anchor: طرحها من شدة الغضب وفرط الضجر حمية للدين

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r7.speaker: رُوي
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r7.claim: A report says the Torah comprised seven portions on seven tablets; after they broke, six sevenths were lifted, containing detailed knowledge, while one seventh remained with exhortations and rulings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r7.anchor: روي: أن التوراة كانت سبعة أسباع في سبعة ألواح فلما ألقاها انكسرت فرفع ستة أسباعها وكان فيها تفصيل كل شيء وبقي سبع كان فيه المواعظ والأحكام.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r8.claim: Moses seized Aaron by the hair and pulled him toward himself, thinking he had failed to restrain them; Aaron was three years older, gentle, and especially beloved by Israel.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r8.anchor: بشعر رأسه. { يجره إليه } توهما بأنه قصر في كفهم، وهارون كان أكبر منه بثلاث سنين وكان حمولا لينا ولذلك كان أحب إلى بني إسرائيل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r9.claim: Calling him “son of my mother” was meant to soften him, though the brothers shared both parents.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r9.anchor: ذكر الأم ليرققه عليه وكانا من أب وأم

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r10.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r10.claim: These readers pronounce “son of my mother” with kasra here and in Ṭā Hā, eliding the yāʾ and relying on kasra for ease.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم هنا وفي «طه» «يا ابن أم» بالكسر وأصله يا ابن أمي فحذفت الياء اكتفاء بالكسرة تخفيفا

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r11.claim: The other readers use fatḥa for greater ease due to the phrase's length or by analogy with khamsata ʿashara.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r11.anchor: والباقون بالفتح زيادة في التخفيف لطوله أو تشبيها بخمسة عشر

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r12.claim: Aaron explains that the people overpowered and weakened him, and nearly killed him, dispelling the idea that he had neglected his duty; he tried all he could to stop them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r12.anchor: إزاحة لتوهم التقصير في حقه، والمعنى بذلت وسعي في كفهم حتى قهروني واستضعفوني وقاربوا قتلي.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r13.claim: “Do not make the enemies gloat over me” means do not do something that would make them rejoice at him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r13.anchor: فلا تفعل بي ما يشمتون بي لأجله

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r14.claim: “Do not count me among the unjust” means do not include him among them by punishing or accusing him of negligence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:150/r14.anchor: معدودا في عدادهم بالمؤاخذة أو نسبة التقصير

SULAMI:v1p244#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r1.claim: Moses grieved that his longing for direct address from the Real had been replaced by speaking to people of no weight, and he was drawn back toward the object of his witnessing.
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r1.anchor: قال : آسفا على ما فاته من مخاطبة الحق إلى مخاطبة من لا أوزان لهم ، فرده من شوقه إلى شاهده

SULAMI:v1p244#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ata says Moses was angry with himself for leaving his people until they went astray and grieved over the loss of intimate conversation with his Lord.
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : غضبان على نفسه حيث ترك قومه حتى ضلوا ، آسفا على مناجاة ربه

SULAMI:v1p244#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r3.claim: Some say Moses reproached himself and regretted losing the privilege of direct address.
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : ماقتا نفسه متأسفا على ما فاته من اختصاصه بالمخاطبة

SULAMI:v1p244#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r4.claim: Some explain that Moses was angered by seeing his people violate God's command.
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : من رأى من قومه من ارتكاب مخالفة الله

SULAMI:v1p244#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r5.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r5.claim: Another explanation says Moses was angered at leaving the direct encounter with the Real to address created beings.
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : اغضبه الرجوع عن مفاجأة الحق إلى مخاطبة الخلق

SULAMI:v1p244#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r6.speaker: القرشي
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r6.claim: Al-Qurashi says God protects those moved by zeal for Him from crossing His limits: Moses was not reproached for throwing the tablets and pulling Aaron because he acted without self-interest, solely from zeal for God, which brought him nearer.
SULAMI:v1p244#2/r6.anchor: قال القرشي : من تحرك غيرة للحق فإن الحق يحفظ عليه حدوده ، لئلا تخرجه الحركة إلى شيء مذموم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p113/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p113/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p113/r7.claim: Moses returned from intimate communion angry and sorrowful because God had informed him that his people worshipped the calf; his anger was for God.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p113/r7.anchor: اي في حال رجوعه لما أخبره الله تعالى عنهم من عبادة العجل

BIQAI-FULL:v3p113/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p113/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p113/r8.claim: Moses calls their succession evil: they occupied his place and acted in his absence in a way that betrayed his trust.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p113/r8.anchor: أي قمتم مقامي وفعلتم مقامي وفعلتم خلفي

BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r1.claim: After me means that they worshipped other than God and failed to restrain the worshippers while Moses went to the mountain for the appointed meeting; successors should follow the one who appointed them.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r1.anchor: أي حيث عبدتم غير الله أيها العبدة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r2.speaker: الصغاني
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r2.claim: Al-Saghani glosses أعجلتم as سبقتم, meaning you preceded or went ahead.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r3.speaker: غيره
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r3.claim: Another lexicographer says عجل عن الأمر means leaving an affair unfinished, while also carrying the sense of preceding.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r3.anchor: وقال غيره : عجل عن الأمر - إذا تركه غير تام , ويضمن معنى سبق

BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r4.speaker: أبو عبد القزاز
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r4.claim: Abu ʿAbd al-Qazzaz also glosses the word as preceding someone; Ibn al-Tayyani attributes this usage to al-Asmaʿi.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r4.anchor: قال الإمام أبو عبد القزاز أيضا : عجلتم : سبقتم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r5.claim: Moses accuses them of assuming he had died and changing the faith as nations changed after their prophets died.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r5.anchor: فنظننتم أني مت فغيرتم كما غيرت المم بعد موت أنبيائها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
