BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r6.claim: He threw down the Torah tablets in anger for God; this shows his anger was so intense that he could not contain himself, and that it was directed toward God's cause.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r6.anchor: أي التي فيها التوراة غضبا لله لقومه

BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r7.claim: Moses seized Aaron by the hair and dragged him to show the people how deeply he was angered by their uprooting of religion.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r7.anchor: يجره إليه } أي بناء على أنه قصر

BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r8.claim: Aaron had not failed to forbid the calf worship; invoking their mother reminded Moses of their bond and called for tenderness toward Aaron, a believer who had endured danger.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r8.anchor: ولما كان هارون عليه السلام غير مقصر في نهيهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r9.claim: In ابن أم, the vocative particle and possessive yā are omitted for brevity suited to the moment.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r9.anchor: وحذف أداة النداء وياء الإضافة لما يقتضيه الحال من الإيجاز

BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r10.claim: The majority read the mīm with fatḥ, treating it like khamsata ʿashar and assuming the alif that replaces the possessive yā was deleted.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r10.anchor: وفتح الجمهور الميم تشبها له بخمسة عشر وعلى حذف الألف المبدلة من ياء لإضافة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r11.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزه والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r11.claim: These readers pronounce the mīm with kasr, on the assumption that the possessive yā was omitted for ease.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r11.anchor: وكسر الميم ابن عامر وحمزه والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم بتقدير حذف ياء افضافة تخفيفا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r12.claim: Aaron says the people intimidated him and nearly killed him for objecting; he asks Moses not to let their enemies rejoice at his humiliation or count him among the wrongdoers.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p114/r12.anchor: لا تسرهم بما تفعل بي فأكون ملوما منهم ومنك

DURR-FULL:v3p560/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r1.claim: The fragment commends truthful speech, keeping promises, honoring trusts, and guarding the hands, eyes, and sexual organs.
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r1.anchor: من حدث فلا يكذب ومن وعد فلا يخلف ومن ائتمن فلا يخون اخفظوا أيديكم وأبصاركم وفروجكم

DURR-FULL:v3p560/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r2.speaker: مالك بن دينار
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r2.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says the Torah teaches that increased knowledge brings increased awe or gravity.
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r2.anchor: عن مالك بن دينار قال: قرأت في التوراة من يزدد علما يزدد وجفا

DURR-FULL:v3p560/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r3.speaker: مالك بن دينار
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r3.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says the Torah treats someone who fails to forbid a sinful neighbor as that neighbor's accomplice.
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r3.anchor: مالك بن دينار قال: قرأت في التوراة من يزدد علما يزدد وجفا وقال: مكتوب في التوراة من كان له جار

DURR-FULL:v3p560/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r4.claim: A Torah saying portrays a person remembering and calling on God while forgetting and fleeing from Him, although God provides for him and he worships another.
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قال: أن في التوراة مكتوبا يا ابن آدم تذكرني وتنساني وتدعو إلي وتفر مني وأرزقك وتعبد غيري

DURR-FULL:v3p560/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r5.speaker: الوليد بن عمر
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r5.claim: A reported Torah saying promises provision when a person works with his hands and urges obedience because God knows what benefits him.
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r5.anchor: عن الوليد بن عمر قال: بلغني أنه مكتوب في التوراة ابن آدم حرك يديك افتح لك بابا من الرزق وأطعني فيما آمرك

DURR-FULL:v3p560/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r6.speaker: عقبة بن زينب
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r6.claim: The Torah warns against relying on mortal people, urges trust in the Living One who never dies, and observes that Moses died, asking who will not die.
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r6.anchor: عن عقبة بن زينب قال: في التوراة مكتوب لا تتوكل على ابن آدم فإن ابن آدم لليس ولكن توكل على الحي الذي لا يموت

DURR-FULL:v3p560/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r7.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r7.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says God loves the one who hates worldly life and honors the one who treats it lightly, while hating and humiliating those who love and honor it.
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r7.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه قال: وجدت فيما أنزل الله على موسى أن من أحب الدنيا أبغضه الله ومن أبغض الدنيا أحبه الله

DURR-FULL:v3p560/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r8.speaker: عروة
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r8.claim: Urwa says the Torah teaches that a pleasant face and kind speech make one more beloved than people who give gifts.
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r8.anchor: عن عروة قال: مكتوب في التوراة ليكن وجهك بسطا وكلمتك طيبة تكن أحب إلى الناس من الذين يعطونهم العطاء

DURR-FULL:v3p560/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r9.speaker: عروة
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r9.claim: Urwa reports a Torah maxim that mercy shown to others is returned in kind.
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r9.anchor: عن عروة قال: بلغني أنه مكتوب في التوراة كما ترحمون ترحمون

DURR-FULL:v3p560/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r10.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r10.claim: Ka'b says the Torah promises longevity and ease and the removal of hardship to one who fears God, honors parents, and maintains kinship.
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r10.anchor: عن كعب قال: والذي فلق البحر لبني إسرائيل في التوراة مكتوب: يا ابن آدم اتق ربك وابرر والديك وصل رحمك

DURR-FULL:v3p560/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r11.speaker: كردوس الثعلبي
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r11.claim: Kurdus al-Tha'labi gives Torah maxims to practice piety, show mercy, and repent so that mercy and acceptance follow.
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r11.anchor: عن كردوس الثعلبي قال: مكتوب في التوراة اتق توقه إنما التوقي في التقوى ارحموا ترحموا توبوا يتاب عليكم

DURR-FULL:v3p560/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r12.speaker: أبو الجوزاء
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r12.claim: Abu al-Jawza says the Torah teaches that someone seeking life and certain knowledge should continually resist worldly desires, driving Satan away.
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r12.anchor: عن أبي الجوزاء قال: قرأت في التوراة أن سرك أن تحيا وتبلغ علم اليقين فاحتمل في كل حين أن تغلب شهوات الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v3p560/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r13.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r13.claim: Ka'b recounts that God had Gabriel bring two tablets from a tree in Paradise, which became light when touched by God and stone when Moses took them; after Moses angrily seized Aaron, Aaron said he feared being blamed for dividing Israel, and Moses sought forgiveness as the tablets shattered.
DURR-FULL:v3p560/r13.anchor: عن كعب قال: لما أراد الله أن يكتب لموسى التوراة قال: يا جبريل ادخل الجنة فائتني بلوحين من شجرة الجنة

DURR-FULL:v3p562/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains asaf as grief or sadness.
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {أسفا} قال: حزينا

DURR-FULL:v3p562/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r9.claim: Qatada says Moses was sad because of what his people did after he left them.
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r9.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا} قال: حزينا على ما صنع قومه من بعده

DURR-FULL:v3p562/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas gives asaf two senses, anger and grief; in 43:55, the related form means they angered God.
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {غضبان اسفا} قال: حزينا وفي الزخرف {فلما آسفونا} الزخرف الآية 55 يقول: اغضبونا

DURR-FULL:v3p562/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r11.claim: Mujahid interprets asaf as distress or anguish.
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {أسفا} قال: جزعا

DURR-FULL:v3p562/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r12.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r12.claim: Abu al-Darda says asaf is a state beyond anger and more intense than it.
DURR-FULL:v3p562/r12.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: الأسف: منزلة وراء الغضب أشد من ذلك

DURR-FULL:v3p564/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p564/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p564/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b says asaf means intense anger.
DURR-FULL:v3p564/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب قال: الأسف: الغضب الشديد

DURR-FULL:v3p564/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p564/r2.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v3p564/r2.claim: The Prophet says seeing is unlike hearing: God told Moses his people had been led astray, but when Moses saw them he cast the tablets and some broke.
DURR-FULL:v3p564/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ايزحم الله موسى ليس المعاين كالمخبر أخبره ربه تبارك وتعالى أن قومه فتنوا بعده

DURR-FULL:v3p564/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p564/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p564/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says Moses's cap would flare like fire when he became angry.
DURR-FULL:v3p564/r3.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم قال: كان موسى عليه السلام إذا غضب اشتعلت قلنسوته نارا

DURR-FULL:v3p564/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p564/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p564/r10.claim: Mujahid explains Moses's plea not to be counted with the wrongdoers as a plea not to be counted with the calf worshippers.
DURR-FULL:v3p564/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {ولا تجعلني مع القوم الظالمين} قال: مع أصحاب العجل

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses Moses' state as angry and sorrowful.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان اسفا يعني الغضبان الحزين

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r2.speaker: الحسن ومالك بن دينار
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r2.claim: Hasan and Malik ibn Dinar are also reported to understand asaf as sorrow.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r2.anchor: وروى عن الحسن ومالك بن دينار مثل ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says asaf has two senses, anger and grief; in 43:55, when God says they angered Him, asaf means they angered Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان اسفا يقول : اسفا حزينا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r4.claim: Mujahid glosses Moses as being deeply distressed.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد غضبان اسفا قال : جزعا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r5.claim: The Prophet says Moses had been told by God that his people were tested, but did not cast down the tablets until he saw them and witnessed their idolatry.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : يرحم الله موسى ليس المعاين كالمخبر

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when Moses threw down the tablets they broke, and all but one sixth of them was raised up.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس : انه لما القى موسى الالواح فتكسرت فرفعت الا سدسها

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says that after throwing the tablets in anger and taking hold of Aaron, Moses excused his brother and sought forgiveness for him.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1569#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : فرجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان اسفا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1570/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1570/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1570/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the wrongdoers Moses asked not to be counted among as the calf worshippers.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1570/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ولا تجعلني مع القوم الظالمين اصحاب العجل

AKHFASH:v1p337/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p337/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p337/r5.claim: ابن أم is treated as a single compound name, like ابن عم أقبل, but Akhfash says this formation is not a general rule.
AKHFASH:v1p337/r5.anchor: وقال {ابن أم إن القوم} . وذلك - والله أعلم - أنه جعله اسما واحدا مثل قولهم "ابن عم أقبل" وهذا لا يقاس عليه [121 ب] .

AKHFASH:v1p337/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p337/r6.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p337/r6.claim: Some propose يا ابن أمي, the regular grammatical form, but Akhfash dislikes it because the written Qur'anic text has no yāʾ.
AKHFASH:v1p337/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم {يا ابن أمي لا تأخذ} وهو القياس ولكن الكتاب ليست فيه ياء فلذلك كره هذا

AKHFASH:v1p337/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p337/r7.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p337/r7.claim: An unidentified poet's khafīf line uses يا ابن أمي as evidence for that expression.
AKHFASH:v1p337/r7.anchor: يا ابن أمي ولو شهدتك إذ تد * عو تميما وأنت غير مجاب

AKHFASH:v1p337/r8.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p337/r8.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p337/r8.claim: Some read يا ابن أم as a dialectal compound with final kasra, like خازباز, or as a single compound name.
AKHFASH:v1p337/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم {ياابن أم} ، فجعله على لغة الذين يقولون هذا غلام قد جاء "أو جعله اسما واحدا آخره مكسور" مثل "خازباز".

AKHFASH:v1p337/r9.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p337/r9.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p337/r9.claim: In يقتلونني the two nūns belong to the verb and attached pronoun; the verb's nūn remains because it is indicative, with plural nūn fatḥa and dual nūn kasra.
AKHFASH:v1p337/r9.anchor: وقال {وكادوا يقتلونني} فثبتت فيه نونان واحدة للفعل والأخرى للاسم المضمر وإنما ثبتت في الفعل لأنه رفع

AKHFASH:v1p337/r10.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p337/r10.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p337/r10.claim: Assimilation or concealment may also occur in this nūn sequence, as in أتعدانني أن أخرج.
AKHFASH:v1p337/r10.anchor: وقد قال {أتعدانني أن أخرج} وقد يجوز في هذا الادغام والاخفاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r1.claim: “You succeeded me” may address Aaron and the leaders, who were Moses’ deputies, and use succession literally.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r1.anchor: وهذا خطاب لهارون ووجوه القوم ، لأنهم خلفاء موسى في قومهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r2.claim: Alternatively, it addresses the entire people: Aaron failed to govern them as Moses did, while the people abandoned Moses’ worship of God for the calf, figuratively failing to follow his example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الخطاب لجميع القوم ، فأما هارون فلأنه لم يحسن الخلافة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r3.claim: Adding “after me” to “you succeeded me” depicts the gulf between them and Moses after his warning against idolatry, including their earlier request for a god like other peoples’ gods.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r3.anchor: وزيادة { من بعدي } عقب { خلفتموني } للتذكير بالبون الشاسع بين حال الخلف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r4.claim: ʿAjila is usually intransitive, meaning to hurry; it can mean failing to complete something begun, or be transitive in the sense of going ahead of something.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r4.anchor: و ( عجل ) أكثر ما يستعمل قاصرا ، بمعنى فعل العجلة أي السرعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r5.claim: One reading of “Have you hastened the command of your Lord?” takes command as God’s obligation to preserve the law and await Moses’ return; the people failed to fulfill it and changed things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r5.anchor: والأمر يكون بمعنى التكليف وهو ما أمرهم الله به : من المحافظة على الشريعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r6.claim: The clearer reading takes “hastened” as going ahead and “command” as the affair of divine anger and threat: they rushed into the prohibited act soon after warning, as if outrunning punishment; 20:86 is parallel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p114/r6.anchor: وهذا هو المعنى الأوضح ، ويوضحه قوله ، في نظير هذه القصة في سورة طه ( 86 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r1.claim: Moses threw the tablets from his hand onto the ground; this indicates they were in his hand when he came down from the divine colloquy, as the Torah explicitly says.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r1.anchor: وذلك يؤذن بأنه لما نزل من المناجاة كانت الألواح في يده كما صرح به في التوراة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r2.claim: The throwing displayed Moses’ anger or resulted from its surge when he saw the people’s state; the Qur’an mentions it for this significance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r2.anchor: ثم إن إلقاءه إياها إنما كان إظهارا للغضب ، أو أثرا من آثار فوران الغضب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r3.claim: The explanation that Moses threw the tablets to free his hand to seize Aaron is unsound: it gives the throwing no lesson and the narrative would have used a causal “then.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r3.anchor: فلا يستقيم قول من فسرها بأن الإلقاء لأجل إشغال يده بجر رأس أخيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r4.claim: An unnamed report describes Moses as quick-tempered and severe in anger, linking this to striking the Egyptian and dragging Aaron; his reaction signals the enormity of the people’s deed, not discipline.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r4.anchor: وروي أن موسى عليه السلام كان في خلقه ضيق ، وكان شديدا عند الغضب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r5.claim: Throwing the tablets was not punishment of the people, since tablets containing what would reform them could not appropriately be treated as prophetic discipline.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r5.anchor: وليس تأديبا لهم ، لأنه لا يكون تأديبهم بإلقاء ألواح كتب فيها ما يصلحهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’ apparent view was that Muhammad refrained from writing the final document to discipline the people for disputing in his presence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r6.anchor: كما هو ظاهر قول ابن عباس ، بل إنما كان ذلك لما رأى من اختلافهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r7.claim: The author rejects that apparent view: Muhammad left the document unwritten because he saw their disagreement and judged it unnecessary for the religion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r7.anchor: بل إنما كان ذلك لما رأى من اختلافهم في ذلك ، فرأى أن الأولى ترك كتابته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r8.speaker: التوراة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r8.claim: The Torah says the tablets broke when Moses threw them; the Qur’an does not state this, though the act of throwing and a report that they were stone suggest breakage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p115/r8.anchor: ووقع في التوراة أن الألواح تكسرت حين ألقاها ، وليس في القرآن ما يدل على ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r1.claim: Aaron’s “they nearly killed me” shows that he resisted them forcefully and then yielded for fear of being killed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { وكادوا يقتلونني } يدل على أنه عارضهم معارضة شديدة ثم سلم خشية القتل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r2.claim: Aaron’s request not to let enemies gloat or count him among wrongdoers follows his explanation and indirectly asks Moses to refrain from punishing him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r2.anchor: طلب من أخيه الكف عن عقابه الذي يشمت به الأعداء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r3.claim: Shamāta is delight at another’s injury, arising from enmity or envy; it is intransitive, has an irregular verbal noun, takes bi for its object, and causative ashmata means to make someone gloat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r3.anchor: والشماتة : سرور النفس بما يصيب غيرها من الإضرار ، وإنما تحصل من العداوة والحسد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r4.claim: Aaron’s “enemies” are the calf worshippers who hated him for opposing them; alternatively, their gloating is an idiom for severe harm whether or not enemies exist.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r4.anchor: وأراد بالأعداء الذين دعوا إلى عبادة العجل ، لأن هارون أنكره عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r5.claim: “Do not make me one of the wrongdoers” may mean do not consider me one of them, with “make” meaning “think,” as at 43:19.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r5.anchor: ف ( جعل ) بمعنى ظن كقوله تعالى : { وجعلوا الملائكة الذين هم عند الرحمن إناثا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, Aaron asks not to be punished with the calf worshippers, whom Moses had ordered killed; here “make” retains its basic sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p117#2/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى : ولا تجعلني في العقوبة معهم

FARRA:v1p393/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p393/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p393/r4.claim: عجلت الشيء means to get ahead of something, whereas أعجلته means to urge or hurry it.

FARRA:v1p393/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p393/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p393/r5.claim: Although Moses broke two tablets, Arabic can use the plural الألواح for two, as with إخوة for two brothers and قلوبكما for two hearts.
FARRA:v1p393/r5.anchor: وجاز أن يقال الألواح للاثنين كما قال فإن كان له إخوة

FARRA:v1p393/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p393/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p393/r6.claim: The frequent vocative ابن أم drops the possessive yāʾ and behaves like an accusative vocative (as in يا حسرتا); this wording softens Aaron, who was Moses’ full brother.
FARRA:v1p393/r6.anchor: وإنما قال له (يا ابن أم) ليستعطفه عليه

FARRA:v1p393/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p393/r7.speaker: مجاهد
FARRA:v1p393/r7.claim: Mujāhid read فلا تشمت بي; al-Kisāʾī wonders whether the intended wording is فلا تشمت بي الأعداء, and says the form may be sound because similar vowel variants occur in Arabic.
FARRA:v1p393/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قرأ (فلا تشمت بي)

FARRA:v1p393/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p393/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p393/r8.claim: In either تشمت or تشمت, الأعداء is nominative because the enemies perform the verb.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r1.claim: Moses returned from the private communion with God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r1.anchor: يريد رجع من المناجاة، ويروى: أنه لما قرب من محلة بني إسرائيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r2.claim: A report says that near Israel’s camp Moses heard idle voices, then became angry and grieved when he confirmed they were devoted to calf worship, and threw the tablets.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r2.anchor: ويروى: أنه لما قرب من محلة بني إسرائيل سمع أصواتهم فقال: هذه أصوات قوم لاهين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r3.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r3.claim: Al-Tabari says God informed Moses before his return that the Israelites had been led astray by the calf, so Moses returned angry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r3.anchor: وقال الطبري: أخبره الله تعالى قبل رجوعه أنهم قد فتنوا بالعجل فلذلك رجع وهو غاضب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r4.claim: أسف can mean intense anger, though it most often means grief; both senses fit here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r4.anchor: و «الأسف» قد يكون بمعنى الغضب الشديد، وأكثر ما يكون بمعنى الحزن والمعنيان مترتبان هاهنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r5.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r5.claim: Al-Kisaʾi analyzes ما attached to بئس as a verbal noun, yielding the sense “evil was your succession after me.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r5.anchor: و «ما» المتصلة ب «بئس» مصدرية، هذا قول الكسائي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r6.claim: To succeed someone with good or evil means to do that to those left behind after him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r6.anchor: ويقال: خلفه بخير أو بشر إذا فعله بمن ترك من بعده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r7.claim: The question أعجلتم means “Did you race God’s decree and make my arrival early, before its appointed time?”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r7.anchor: فقوله: أعجلتم معناه: أسابقتم قضاء ربكم واستعجلتم إتياني قبل الوقت الذي قدر به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Moses threw the tablets because he was angry at the Israelites’ calf worship and at Aaron for neglecting to stop them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r8.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس: كان سبب إلقائه الألواح غضبه على قومه في عبادتهم العجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r9.claim: Qatada, if the report is sound, says Moses saw the virtues of Muhammad’s community on the tablets, wanted them for his own community, and grew angry when told they belonged to another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة إن صح عنه: بل كان ذلك لما رأى فيها من فضيلة أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls Qatada’s explanation bad and says it should not be attributed to Moses; he holds the first explanation correct.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r10.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا قول رديء لا ينبغي أن يوصف موسى عليه السلام به والأول هو الصحيح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Moses had a sharp temperament, a trait established elsewhere.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r11.anchor: وبالجملة فكان في خلق موسى عليه السلام ضيق وذلك مستقر في غير موضع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r12.claim: The tablets are said to have been two boards, with a plural used for the dual.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r12.anchor: وروي أنها كانت لوحان وجمع إذ التثنية جمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r13.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r13.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas says the tablets were a load of seventy camels and could be read a portion at a time over a year; the author calls this weak and excessive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r13.anchor: وروي أنها كانت وقر سبعين بعيرا يقرأ منها الجزء في سنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the tablets broke when Moses cast them down; the largest portion, containing an explanation of everything, was lifted, and the remaining portion with guidance and mercy was later taken up.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إن موسى لما ألقاها تكسرت فرفع أكثرها الذي فيه تفصيل كل شيء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r15.claim: Taking Aaron by the head and beard is the apparent meaning of the wording.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r15.anchor: وأخذه برأس أخيه ولحيته من الخلق المذكور، هذا ظاهر اللفظ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r16.claim: Another report says Moses took Aaron aside to speak privately; Aaron feared onlookers would assume anger and therefore pleaded with him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p456#2/r16.anchor: وروي أن ذلك إنما كان ليساره فخشي هارون أن يتوهم الناظر إليهما أنه لغضب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects the report that Moses merely took Aaron aside to speak and prefers the literal angry seizure, citing Aaron’s reminder that Moses left Israel divided and ignored his counsel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا ضعيف، والأول هو الصحيح لقوله رقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r2.claim: Calling Aaron ابن أم is an affectionate appeal to their shared mother, the closest kinship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r2.anchor: وقوله: ابن أم استلطاف برحم الأم إذ هو ألصق القرابات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r3.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r3.claim: They read ابن أم with fatḥa on the mīm; Kufan grammarians derive it from ابن أماه with deletion for ease, while Sibawayh treats the two words as a compound like خمسة عشر.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم «ابن أم» بفتح الميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r4.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r4.claim: They read ابن أم with kasra on mīm, as if the original were ابن أمي; the yaʾ may be deleted for ease or through compounding, the latter being Sibawayh’s more sound account.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي «ابن أم» بكسر الميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r5.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r5.claim: For the kasra reading, Sibawayh’s compound-word analysis is more measured than simple deletion for ease; after adding to the speaker’s yaʾ, the yaʾ is dropped as in the vocative يا غلام.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r5.anchor: وهذا أقيس من الحذف تخفيفا، ثم أضافوا إلى ياء المتكلم، ثم حذفت الياء من أمي على لغة من يقول يا غلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r6.claim: Without treating ابن أم as a compound, deleting the possessive yaʾ would not be valid because “mother” is not being called directly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r6.anchor: ولو لم يقدر جعل الأول والآخر اسما واحدا لما صح حذفها لأن الأم ليست بمناداة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r7.claim: استضعفوني means they considered me weak.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r8.claim: كادوا means they nearly did it, but did not actually do it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r8.anchor: وقوله: كادوا معناه قاربوا ولم يفعلوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r9.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r9.claim: The majority read فلا تشمت with taʾ damma and mīm kasra, and الأعداء in the accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r9.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «فلا تشمت بي الأعداء» بضم التاء وكسر الميم ونصب الأعداء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r10.speaker: مجاهد فيما حكاه أبو حاتم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r10.claim: Mujahid’s first transmitted reading opens taʾ and mīm and puts الأعداء in the nominative, meaning “do not let them gloat because of something you do to me.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r10.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد فيما حكاه أبو حاتم «فلا تشمت بي» بفتح التاء من فوق والميم ورفع «الأعداء»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r11.speaker: حميد بن قيس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r11.claim: Humayd ibn Qays reads with open taʾ, kasra on mīm, and الأعداء nominative; Abu Hatim transmits it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r11.anchor: وقرأ حميد بن قيس «تشمت» بتاء مفتوحة وميم مكسورة ورفع «الأعداء» حكاها أبو حاتم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r12.speaker: مجاهد فيما حكاه أبو الفتح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r12.claim: Another Mujahid reading opens taʾ and mīm but leaves الأعداء accusative; Abu al-Fath parses it as addressing God, then ellipsing a verb for the enemies.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r12.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد أيضا فيما حكاه أبو الفتح «فلا تشمت بي الأعداء» بفتح التاء من فوق والميم ونصب الأعداء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r13.speaker: أبو الفتح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r13.claim: He explains the open-taʾ reading as “You, Lord, do not gloat over me,” then returns to the intended sense by supplying an omitted verb governing الأعداء.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r13.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: فلا تشمت بي أنت يا رب، وجاز هذا كما قال تعالى: يستهزئ بهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls Abu al-Fath’s grammatical explanation strained.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r14.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وفي كلام أبي الفتح هذا تكلف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r15.speaker: المهدوي عن ابن محيصن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p457/r15.claim: Al-Mahdawi introduces a reading from Ibn Muhaysin that is given in the next segment.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p458/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p458/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p458/r1.claim: Schadenfreude is an enemy’s joy at the misfortune of an enemy.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p458/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p458/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p458/r2.claim: The wrongdoing people Aaron asks not to be grouped with are the worshippers of the calf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p458/r2.anchor: وقوله: ولا تجعلني مع القوم الظالمين يريد عبدة العجل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r1.claim: One explanation of asaf is grief; al-Hasan and al-Suddi share this view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r1.anchor: أحدها أنه الحزين قاله ابن عباس والحسن والسدي والثاني الجزع قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r2.anchor: أحدها أنه الحزين قاله ابن عباس والحسن والسدي والثاني الجزع قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba and al-Zajjaj explain asaf as intense anger.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r3.anchor: والثالث أنه الشديد الغضب قاله ابن قتيبة والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r4.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Darda says asaf is a state beyond anger and more severe than it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء الأسف منزلة وراء الغضب أشد منه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r5.claim: The Hijaz readers and Abu Amr pronounce the ya in baʿdi with fatḥa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r5.anchor: فتح ياء بعدي أهل الحجاز وأبو عمرو والمعنى بئس ما عملتم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r6.claim: Moses rebukes them for worshipping the calf after he left them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r6.anchor: والمعنى بئس ما عملتم بعد فراقي من عبادة العجل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r7.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r7.claim: Al-Farra distinguishes ʿajiltu the matter as getting ahead of it from aʿjaltuhu as urging it on.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r7.anchor: قال الفراء يقال عجلت الأمر والشيء سبقته ومنه هذه الآية وأعجلته استحثثته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas understands the question as asking why they hastened their Lord's appointed time instead of waiting.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس أعجلتم ميعاد ربكم فلم تصبروا له

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the appointment as the promised forty nights.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r9.anchor: قال الحسن يعني وعد الأربعين ليلة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r10.claim: One account says Moses threw the tablets in anger on seeing the people worship the calf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r10.anchor: أحدهما أنه الغضب حين رآهم قد عبدوا العجل قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r11.claim: Qatada says Moses threw them after seeing another community's virtues, but Ibn al-Jawzi considers this explanation remote.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r11.anchor: والثاني أنه لما رأى فضائل غير أمته من أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم اشتد عليه فألقاها قاله قتادة وفيه بعد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says the shattered tablets lost six sevenths, with one seventh remaining.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p263#2/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس لما رمى بالألواح فتحطمت رفع منها ستة أسباع وبقي سبع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r1.claim: One reported view says Moses seized Aaron by his beard and forelock.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r1.anchor: في ما أخذ به من رأسه ثلاثة أقوال أحدها لحيته وذؤابته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r2.claim: Other reported views say Moses seized Aaron's head hair or his ear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r2.anchor: والثاني شعر رأسه والثالث أذنه وقيل إنما فعل به ذلك لأنه توهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r3.claim: Moses thought Aaron had disobeyed by staying with the people instead of following him and reporting their new act, so he could return and correct them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r3.anchor: تعريفه ما أحدثوا بعده ليرجع إليهم فيتلافاهم ويردهم إلى الحق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Abu Amr, and Hafs read ibn umm with an accusative ending and an open mim.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم قال ابن أم نصبا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r5.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Abu Bakr read the mim with kasra, as in Ta Ha.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم بكسر الميم وكذلك في طه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the open form reflects frequent use of this name, while the kasra makes an annexation after treating the words as one name.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج من فتح الميم فلكثرة استعمال هذا الاسم ومن كسر أضافه إلى نفسه بعد أن جعله اسما واحدا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r7.claim: An unnamed poet retains the ya in the vocative phrase ibn ummi, addressing Moses as a brother and successor in hardship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r7.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول يا ابن أمي بإثبات الياء قال الشاعر يا ابن أمي ويا شقيق نفسي أنت خليفتي لدهر شديد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r8.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r8.claim: Abu Ali offers two analyses: the open reading drops the alif of umma, and the kasra reading drops the ya of ummi.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r8.anchor: قال أبو علي يحتمل أن يريد من فتح يا ابن أم أما ويحذف الألف ومن كسر ابن أمي فيحذف الياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says Aaron was Moses' full brother and Moses used the maternal address to soften him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r9.anchor: أن ابن عباس قال كان أخاه لأبيه وأمه وإنما قال له ذلك ليرفقه عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r10.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r10.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi says mentioning one's mother softens a person more than mentioning one's father.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r10.anchor: قال أبو سليمان الدمشقي والإنسان عند ذكر الوالدة أرق منه عند ذكر الوالد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r11.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r11.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi reports a contrasting view that Aaron was Moses' maternal brother but not his paternal brother.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p264/r11.anchor: وقيل كان لأمه دون أبيه حكاه الثعلبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r1.claim: The people who had weakened Aaron were the calf worshippers, and they had humiliated him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r1.anchor: يعني عبدة العجل ﴿ استضعفوني ﴾ أي استذلوني

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Malik ibn Dinar, and Ibn Asim read the verb with open ta and mim and read al-aʿdaʾ in the nominative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r2.anchor: قرأ عبد الله بن عباس ومالك بن دينار وابن عاصم فلا تشمت بتاء مفتوحة مع فتح الميم الاعداء بالرفع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r3.claim: Mujahid, Abu al-Aliya, al-Dahhak, and Abu Raja read the verb with open ta and kasra on mim, with al-aʿdaʾ in the accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r3.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وأبو العالية والضحاك وأبو رجاء فلا تشمت بفتح التاء وكسر الميم الأعداء بالنصب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r4.claim: Abu al-Jawza and Ibn Abi Abla use that same verb reading but put al-aʿdaʾ in the nominative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو الجوزاء وابن أبي عبلة مثل ذلك إلا أنهما رفعا الأعداء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r5.claim: The enemies Aaron asks not to be gladdened are the calf worshippers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r5.anchor: إلا أنهما رفعا الأعداء ويعني بالاعداء عبدة العجل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r6.claim: Aaron asks Moses not to count him among the wrongdoers in his anger and punishment of him; the wrongdoers are the calf worshippers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p265/r6.anchor: في موجدتك وعقوبتك لي ﴿ مع القوم الظالمين ﴾ وهم عبدة العجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r1.claim: Abu al-Darda explains أسف as the most intense anger.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r2.claim: Moses rebukes them for the evil way they succeeded him by worshipping the calf after he left.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r2.anchor: يقول: بئس ما صنعتم في عبادتكم العجل بعد أن ذهبت وتركتكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r3.claim: Moses asks why they hastened his return; its timing had been decreed by God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r3.anchor: يقول: استعجلتم مجيئي إليكم، وهو مقدر من الله تعالى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r4.claim: One reported view says the tablets were made of emerald.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r5.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r5.claim: Another reported view says the tablets were made of ruby.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r6.claim: A further reported view says the tablets were made of ice.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r7.claim: The material reports illustrate the principle that direct observation is unlike merely hearing a report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r7.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على ما جاء في الحديث: "ليس الخبر كالمعاينة"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r8.speaker: جمهور العلماء سلفا وخلفا
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r8.claim: The apparent sequence is that Moses threw the tablets in anger at his people; Ibn Kathir endorses this as the majority view of early and later scholars.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r8.anchor: وهذا قول جمهور العلماء سلفا وخلفا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects the strange report attributed by al-Tabari to Qatada as an unsound attribution, likely taken from unreliable People of the Book; Ibn Atiyya and others also reject it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p476#2/r9.anchor: وروى ابن جرير عن قتادة في هذا قولا غريبا، لا يصح إسناده إلى حكاية قتادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r1.claim: Moses grabs Aaron because he fears Aaron failed to restrain the people; the parallel account in Ṭā Hā explains Aaron feared Moses would accuse him of dividing Israel or disobeying.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r1.anchor: خوفا أن يكون قد قصر في نهيهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r2.claim: Aaron's address ‘son of my mother’ is meant to make Moses more tender and responsive, though Aaron was his full brother.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r3.claim: Aaron asks Moses not to delight their enemies or count him among the wrongdoers, meaning not to treat him as one of them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r3.anchor: أي: لا تسقني مساقهم، ولا تخلطني معهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r5.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r5.claim: The Prophet says Moses did not throw the tablets when God informed him that his people had fallen into trial; seeing them himself moved him to throw them, for seeing is unlike hearing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p477/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال النبي (4) صلى الله عليه وسلم "يرحم (5) الله موسى، ليس المعاين كالمخبر

JISHUMI:v4p2705/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2705/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2705/r2.claim: Moses appointed Aaron in his absence because the people obeyed and accepted Aaron more readily.
JISHUMI:v4p2705/r2.anchor: وتدل على أنه استخلف هارون عند خروجه لما رأى أنهم أشد طاعة له وأكثر قبولا منه،

JISHUMI:v4p2705/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2705/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2705/r3.claim: Their exchange suggests that Moses had a distinct authority even though both brothers were prophets; his deputyship lasted until his return.
JISHUMI:v4p2705/r3.anchor: ومخاطبات موسى (عليه السلام) وجوابه له لقوله: (أفعصيت أمري) وقول هارون: (لا تأخذ بلحيتي) (فلا تشمت بي الأعداء) كل ذلك كالدال على أن موسى كان يختص بنوع من الولاية، وإن اشتركا في النبوة، والظاهر أنه استخلفه إلى أن يرجع؛ لأنه المعقول من الاستخلاف عند الغيبة.

JISHUMI:v4p2705/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2705/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2705/r4.claim: It is permissible to forbid what one knows a person will not do, or command what one knows they will do, to admonish, teach others, and secure a shared benefit.
JISHUMI:v4p2705/r4.anchor: وتدل على أنه يجوز أن ينهاه عن شيء يعلم أنه لا يفعله، ولأمره بما يعلم أنه سيفعله؛ عظة له واعتبارا لغيره، وتأكيدا ومصلحة للجميع.

JISHUMI:v4p2724/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2724/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2724/r6.claim: The verse narrates Moses returning angry and grieving, rebuking the people, casting down the tablets, and pulling Aaron toward him.
JISHUMI:v4p2724/r6.anchor: قوله تعالى: (ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال بئسما خلفتموني من بعدي أعجلتم أمر ربكم وألقى الألواح وأخذ برأس أخيه يجره إليه

JISHUMI:v4p2724/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2724/r14.speaker: العامة
JISHUMI:v4p2724/r14.claim: The general reading has taʾḍmit with ḍamma on tāʾ and kasra on mīm, with “the enemies” as its accusative object.
JISHUMI:v4p2724/r14.anchor: والقراءة الظاهرة: فلا تشمت بضم التاء وكسر الميم الأعداء نصب على أنه مفعول،

JISHUMI:v4p2724/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2724/r15.speaker: مجاهد ومالك بن دينار
JISHUMI:v4p2724/r15.claim: Mujahid and Malik ibn Dinar read with fatḥa on tāʾ and mīm, making “the enemies” the subject who gloat.
JISHUMI:v4p2724/r15.anchor: وعن مجاهد ومالك بن دينار ([فلا] تشمت) بفتح التاء والميم، والأعداء رفع على أن الفعل مضاف إليهم.

NAHHAS:v2p151/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p151/r3.claim: Ghadban is an accusative circumstantial and a diptote because its feminine is ghadba; its nūn substitutes for the feminine alif as in hamra and Sanʿani.
NAHHAS:v2p151/r3.anchor: نصب على الحال ولم ينصرف لأن مؤنثه غضبى وحقيقة امتناع صرفه أن الألف والنون فيه بمنزلة ألفي التأنيث

NAHHAS:v2p151/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r4.speaker: يعقوب
NAHHAS:v2p151/r4.claim: Yaʿqub says ʿajiltu al-shayʾ means I drove it on, whereas aʿjaltu al-rajul means I made the man hurry.
NAHHAS:v2p151/r4.anchor: قال يعقوب يقال عجلت الشيء سقته وأعجلت الرجل استعجلته

NAHHAS:v2p151/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p151/r5.claim: Taking someone by the head and taking his head are equivalent expressions here.

NAHHAS:v2p151/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p151/r6.claim: One view says Moses took Aaron aside only to confer privately; Aaron feared witnesses would misunderstand, since matters were otherwise.
NAHHAS:v2p151/r6.anchor: وقيل إنما أخذ برأسه على جهة المسارة لا غير فكره هارون صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يتوهم من حضر

NAHHAS:v2p151/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p151/r7.claim: Calling him son of his mother appeals to their shared maternal kinship; an anonymous Arabic line illustrates this address.
NAHHAS:v2p151/r7.anchor: فقال ابن أم على الاستعطاف له لأنه أخوه لأمه وهذا موجود في كلام العرب

NAHHAS:v2p151/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p151/r8.claim: The reading of ibn umm is assigned to the Medinans and Abu ʿAmr, and separately to the Kufans; the excerpt prints no visible vowel contrast.
NAHHAS:v2p151/r8.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو ( ابن أم إن القوم ) وقرأ أهل الكوفة ( ابن أم إن القوم )

NAHHAS:v2p151/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r9.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v2p151/r9.claim: Al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ, and Abū ʿUbayd parse yā ibn umm as yā ibn ummāh, with the vocative alif retained in the estimate.
NAHHAS:v2p151/r9.anchor: قال الكسائي والفراء وأبو عبيد يا ابن أم تقديره يا ابن أماه

NAHHAS:v2p151/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r10.speaker: البصريون
NAHHAS:v2p151/r10.claim: The Basran grammarians reject that account: the light alif is not deleted, and the two words instead form one compound, like khamsata ʿashara.
NAHHAS:v2p151/r10.anchor: وقال البصريون هذا القول خطأ لأن الألف خفيفة لا تحذف ولكن جعل الاسمان اسما واحدا فصار كقولك خمسة عشر

NAHHAS:v2p151/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r11.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v2p151/r11.claim: Al-Akhfash and Abū Ḥātim compare yā ibn umm with the anomalous doubled vocative yā ghulāmu ghulām.
NAHHAS:v2p151/r11.anchor: وقال الأخفش وأبو حاتم يا ابن أم كما يقول يا غلام غلام أقبل

NAHHAS:v2p151/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r12.speaker: أبو جعفر
NAHHAS:v2p151/r12.claim: Abū Jaʿfar finds the doubled ghulām form anomalous and the mīm-kasra reading distant on that basis, but prefers treating the words as one compound vocative like khamsata ʿashara.
NAHHAS:v2p151/r12.anchor: قال أبو جعفر يا غلام غلام لغة شاذة لأن الثاني ليس بمنادي

NAHHAS:v2p151/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p151/r13.claim: Istadaʿfūnī and kādū yaqtulūnanī retain two nūns because they are imperfect verbs; assimilation is permissible outside Qurʾānic recitation.
NAHHAS:v2p151/r13.anchor: أضاف ( إن القوم استضعفوني وكادوا يقتلونني ) بنونين لأنه فعل مستقبل ويجوز الادغام

NAHHAS:v2p151/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r14.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v2p151/r14.claim: Mujāhid and Mālik ibn Dīnār read tushmit as a feminine collective; masculine agreement is also possible for the plural enemies.
NAHHAS:v2p151/r14.anchor: قرأ مجاهد ومالك بن دينار ( فلا تشمت بي الأعداء ) بالتاء على تأنيث الجماعة

NAHHAS:v2p151/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p151/r15.claim: The prohibition asks the enemies not to make Aaron a cause for their gloating, like the command to remain Muslim until death comes; it parallels Arab lā arīnnaka hāhunā.
NAHHAS:v2p151/r15.anchor: يقال كيف نهى الأعداء عن الشماتة فالجواب أن هذا مثل قوله جل وعز فلا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون

NAHHAS:v2p151/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p151/r16.speaker: أبو عبيد
NAHHAS:v2p151/r16.claim: Abū ʿUbayd transmits Ḥumayd's mīm-kasra reading, but Abū Jaʿfar rejects it because neither the three-letter nor causative verb has that form.
NAHHAS:v2p151/r16.anchor: قال أبو عبيد وحكيت عن حميد ( فلا تشمت ) بكسر الميم قال أبو جعفر ولا وجه لهذه القراءة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r1.claim: Asaf means intense anger, as in the linked verse about God's anger and punishment; another view takes it to mean grief.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r1.anchor: الأسف : الشديد الغضب { فلما ءاسفونا انتقمنا منهم } ( الزخرف : 55 ) وقيل : هو الحزين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r2.claim: Khalafتموني means you took my place as my successors after me.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r2.anchor: خلفتمونى } قمتم مقامي وكنتم خلفائي من بعدي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r3.claim: The address may target the calf-worshipping Samaritan and his followers, or Israel's leaders, including Aaron and the believers among them; the latter is supported by Moses' earlier charge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r3.anchor: وهذا الخطاب إما أن يكون لعبدة العجل من السامري وأشياعه أو لوجوه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r4.claim: The blame is for replacing God's worship with the calf, or for failing to restrain those who worshipped something other than God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى : بئس ما خلفتموني حيث عبدتم العجل مكان عبادة الله ، أو حيث

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r5.claim: In the grammar of biʾs, the subject is implicit and explained by mā khalafتمūnī; the omitted object of blame is their bad succession.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r5.anchor: الفاعل مضمر يفسره ما خلفتموني . والمخصوص بالذم محذوف تقديره : بئس خلافة خلفتمونيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r6.claim: 'After me' means after witnessing Moses affirm God's oneness, reject partners, and purify worship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r6.anchor: معناه من بعد ما رأيتم مني ، من توحيد الله ، ونفي الشركاء عنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, it means after Moses had kept Israel committed to monotheism and restrained their desire for a calf, recalled by their earlier request for a god.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r7.anchor: أو من بعد ما كنت أحمل بني إسرائيل على التوحيد . وأكفهم عما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r8.claim: A successor should follow the predecessor's way rather than contradict it; the linked verse likewise speaks of later successors after praiseworthy predecessors.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r8.anchor: ومن حق الخلفاء أن يسيروا بسيرة المستخلف من بعده ولا يخالفوه . ونحوه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r9.claim: ʿAjila ʿan al-amr means to leave a matter unfinished; its opposite is to complete it, and it can be made transitive by implication of 'precede'.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r9.anchor: يقال : عجل عن الأمر إذا تركه غير تام ، ونقيضه تم عليه وأعجله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r10.claim: Moses asks whether Israel hastened past God's command instead of awaiting him and keeping his charge, supposing the appointment ended and he would not return.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r10.anchor: والمعنى أعجلتم عن أمر ربكم ، وهو انتظار موسى حافظين لعهده وما وصاكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r11.claim: One report says the Samaritan told them Moses had died and would not return when he displayed the calf.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r11.anchor: وروي : أن السامري قال لهم حين أخرج لهم العجل وقال هذا إلاهكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r12.claim: Another report says they counted twenty days and nights as forty, then committed their deed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r12.anchor: وروي : أنهم عدوا عشرين يوما بلياليها فجعلوها أربعين ، ثم أحدثوا ما أحدثوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r13.claim: Moses cast the tablets down in shock and distress on hearing of the calf, out of anger for God and zeal for His religion.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r13.anchor: وألقى الالواح } وطرحها لما لحقه من فرط الدهش وشدة الضجر عند استماعه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r14.claim: Moses was quick-tempered, while Aaron was gentler and therefore more loved by Israel.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r14.anchor: وكان في نفسه حديدا شديد الغضب ، وكان هارون ألين منه جانبا ولذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r15.claim: A report says the Torah had seven parts; after the tablets broke, six sevenths were lifted and one remained, containing all details and mercy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r15.anchor: وروى : أن التوراة كانت سبعة أسباع ، فلما ألقى الألواح تكسرت فرفع منها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r16.claim: Taking Aaron by the head means by his hair, dragging him by the forelock in the shock that clouded Moses' judgment as he suspected Aaron had failed to restrain the people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r16.anchor: وأخذ برأس أخيه } أي بشعر رأسه { يجره إليه } بذؤابته وذلك لشدة ما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r17.claim: Ibn umm is read with fatḥa by analogy to khamsata ʿashara, with kasra by dropping the possessive yāʾ, also as ibn ummī with yāʾ and ibn imm with kasra on both letters.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r17.anchor: ابن أم } قرىء بالفتح تشبيها بخمسة عشر ، وبالكسر على طرح ياء الإضافة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r18.claim: Some say Aaron was Moses' full brother; if so, Moses invoked their shared mother to awaken tenderness, stress their bond, and honor their believing mother and her suffering.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r18.anchor: وقيل : كان أخاه لأبيه وأمه ، فإن صح فإنما أضافه إلى الأم ، إشارة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r19.claim: Aaron says he did all he could through warning and admonition, but the people overpowered and weakened him and nearly killed him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r19.anchor: إن القوم } يعني أنه لم يأل جهدا في كفهم بالوعظ والإنذار . وبما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r20.claim: Moses is asked not to do what the enemies hoped for by humiliating or mistreating Aaron; a reading instead addresses the enemies, forbidding them to rejoice.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r20.anchor: فلا تشمت بى الاعداء } فلا تفعل بي ما هو أمنيتهم من الاستهانة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r21.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r21.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r21.claim: Aaron asks not to be grouped with the wrongdoers in Moses' anger and punishment, or not to be regarded as one of them despite his innocence.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p152#2/r21.anchor: ولا تجعلنى مع القوم الظالمين } ولا تجعلني في موجدتك علي وعقوبتك لي

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r1.speaker: علي بن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r1.claim: Asaf can mean regret over what has passed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r1.anchor: أنه المتأسف على فوت ما سلف قاله علي بن عيسى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses asaf as grief.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r3.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses asaf as intense anger.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r4.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r4.claim: Al-Suddi glosses asaf as being incensed.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses asaf as remorse.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r6.claim: One reading is that Moses was angry with his people for worshipping the calf and grieved over missing his communion with God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r6.anchor: غضبان من قومه على عبادة العجل ؟ أسفا على ما فاته من مناجاة ربه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r7.claim: Alternatively, Moses was angry with himself for leaving his people, and grieved at their sins after he saw them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r7.anchor: غضبان على نفسه في ترك قومه حتى ضلوا , أسفا على ما رأى في قومه من ارتكاب المعاصي

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r8.speaker: بعض المتصوفة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r8.claim: Some Sufis say he was angry at leaving communion with the Real to address created beings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r8.anchor: إن غضبه للرجوع عن مناجاة الحق إلى مخاطبة الخلق

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r9.claim: Moses says they were a bad replacement because they worshipped the calf after him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r10.speaker: الحسن والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r10.claim: They explain the hastening as abandoning Moses' promised forty nights because the people thought he had died when he missed the thirtieth night.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r10.anchor: وذلك أنه قدروا أنه قد مات لما لم يأت على رأس الثلاثين ليلة , قاله الحسن , والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r11.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r11.claim: A later view says they hastened God's promise of reward for worship by turning to worship another instead.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r11.anchor: وعد ربكم بالثواب على عبادته حتى عدلتم إلى عبادة غيره , قاله بعض المتأخرين

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r12.claim: Ajala means doing something before its time, while surʿa means doing it in less time.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r12.anchor: الفرق بين العجلة والسرعة أن العجلة : التقدم بالشيء قبل وقته , والسرعة : عمله في أقل أوقاته

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r13.claim: Moses threw the tablets in anger when he saw the people worshipping the calf.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r13.anchor: غضبا حين رأى عبادة العجل , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r14.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r14.claim: Qatada says Moses saw the virtues of Muhammad's community, asked that they be his community, and threw the tablets in anguish when told they were Ahmad's community.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r14.anchor: قال : تلك أمة أحمد , فاشتد عليه فألقاها , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r15.claim: The Torah had seven parts; six were lifted after the tablets broke, leaving guidance and mercy in the remaining seventh.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r15.anchor: وكانت التوراة سبعة أسباع فلما ألقى موسى الألواح فتكسرت رفع منها ستة أسباعها

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas says the tablets broke and all but one sixth was taken up.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r16.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : ألقى موسى الألواح فتكسرت ورفعت إلا سدسها

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r17.claim: The phrase about taking Aaron by the head has two readings: Moses took his ear, or his whole head.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r17.anchor: أحدهما : أنه أخذ بأذنه . والثاني : أخذ بجملة رأسه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r18.claim: One answer is that custom changes whether such an act counts as humiliating, and it may not have been humiliating then.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r18.anchor: أن هذا الفعل مما قد يتغير حكمه بالعادة فيجوز أن يكون في ذلك الزمان بخلاف ما هو عليه الآن من الهوان

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r19.claim: Another answer compares Moses' action to someone now taking hold of his beard or biting his lip.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r19.anchor: أن ذلك منه كقبض الرجل منا الآن على لحيته وعضه على شفته

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r20.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r20.claim: Moses called Aaron son of his mother because Aaron was his maternal brother.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r20.anchor: لأنه كان أخاه لأمه , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r21.claim: Alternatively, this is an Arab expression appealing to kinship to soften the listener.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p262/r21.anchor: على عادة العرب استعطافا بالرحم , كما قال الشاعر :

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p264/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p264/r1.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p264/r1.claim: A poetic address, son of my mother and twin of my soul, illustrates the appeal to kinship in Aarons plea.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p264/r1.anchor: يا ابن أمي ويا شقيق نفسي … أنت خليتني لأمر شديد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p264/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p264/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p264/r2.claim: The enemies are those who opposed Aaron over the calf worship; their opposition made them his enemies.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p264/r2.anchor: يعني من خالفه في عبادة العجل لأنهم قد صاروا لمخالفتهم له أعداء

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p264/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p264/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p264/r3.claim: Aaron asks Moses not to be angry with him as with the wrongdoers, since he was not one of them; this softened Moses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p264/r3.anchor: أي لا تغضب علي كغضبك عليهم ولست منهم فأدركته الرقة

MUJAHID:v1p247/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p247/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p247/r1.claim: Moses asks not to be grouped with the wrongdoers, meaning the people of the calf.
MUJAHID:v1p247/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ولا تجعلني مع القوم الظالمين ﴾ قال يعني مع أصحاب العجل

MUQATIL:7:150-151/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:150-151/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:150-151/r1.claim: Moses returned from the mountain angry and sorrowful over his people's calf worship, of which God had informed him on the Mount.
MUQATIL:7:150-151/r1.anchor: يعني حزينا في صنع قومه في عبادة العجل

MUQATIL:7:150-151/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:150-151/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:150-151/r2.claim: Moses rebuked his people for hastening their Lord's command by rushing the forty-day appointment.

MUQATIL:7:150-151/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:150-151/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:150-151/r3.claim: Moses threw the tablets from his shoulder; five were lost and four remained.
MUQATIL:7:150-151/r3.anchor: من عاتقه، فذهب منها خمس وبقيت أربعة

MUQATIL:7:150-151/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:150-151/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:150-151/r4.claim: Moses seized Aaron by the head and dragged him toward himself; Aaron said the people had overpowered him and nearly killed him, and asked Moses not to let enemies gloat or count him among wrongdoers.
MUQATIL:7:150-151/r4.anchor: يعني إلى نفسه، { قال } هارون لموسى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r1.claim: Moses returned from the mountain to the Israelites angry and grieved; غضبان and أسفا are both circumstantial phrases.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r1.anchor: حال من مسوى ﴿ أسفا ﴾ حال أيضا أى حزينا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r2.claim: خلفتموني means you succeeded me in my place and acted as my deputies.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r3.claim: The rebuke may address the calf worshippers, the Samaritan and his followers, or Aaron and the believers with him; اخلفني in 7:142 supports the latter possibility.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r3.anchor: والخكطاب لبعدة العجل من السامرى وأشياعه أو لهرون ونم معه من المؤمنين

NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r4.claim: The blame is for worshipping the calf in place of God, or for failing to stop worship of anything besides God; the omitted object of blame is their bad succession.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r4.anchor: بئسما خلفتمونى حيث عبدتم العجل مكان عبادة الله أو حيث لم تكفوا عن عبادة غير الله

NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r5.claim: من بعدي can mean after witnessing Moses' monotheism and rejection of partners, or after he had kept Israel devoted to monotheism; they had previously asked for a god like other people's gods (7:138).
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r5.anchor: من بعد ما رأيتم منى من توحيد الله ونفى الشركاء عنه أو من بعد ما كنت احمل بنى إسرائيل على التوحيد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r6.claim: أعجلتم means “did you hasten?” by worshipping the calf; أمر ربكم is God's appointment to give the Torah after forty nights, and haste is seeking something before its time.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r6.anchor: وهو ايتانى لكم بالتوارة بعد أربعين ليلة وأصل العجلة طلب الشئ قبل حينه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r7.claim: Another interpretation takes عجلتم to mean “did you abandon?”

NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r8.claim: Moses threw the tablets in anger for God's sake; his naturally intense anger contrasts with Aaron's gentler disposition, which made Aaron more beloved to Israel. They broke: six sevenths were removed and one seventh remained, the removed portion containing detailed knowledge and the remainder guidance and mercy.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r8.anchor: ضجرا عند استماعه حديث العجل غضبا لله كان فى نفسه شجديد الغضب وكان هرون أبين منه جانبا ولذلك كان أحب إلى بنى إسرائيل من موسى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r9.claim: He took Aaron by the hair on his head and dragged him in anger because Aaron did not stop the calf worship, rebuking him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r9.anchor: بشعر رأسه غضبا عليه حيث لم يمنعهم عن عبادة العجل

NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r10.claim: ابن أم is a compound; Hamza, Ali, and the Shami reader pronounce the م with kasra because the original ي was deleted and its kasra retained. Although Aaron shared both parents, the mother is named because she believed and her mention invites compassion.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r10.anchor: وشامى لأن أصله امى فحذف الياء اجتزاء عنها بالكسرة وكان ابن أمه وأبيه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r11.claim: Aaron says he tried his utmost through admonition and warning, but the people overpowered him and nearly killed him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r11.anchor: أى إنى لم آل جهدا فى كفهم بالوعظ والإنذار ولكنهم استضعفونى وهموا بقتلى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r12.claim: The enemies are the calf worshippers; Moses should not do what they wish by humiliating or harming Aaron, or treat him as one of the wrongdoers by sharing his anger with them.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p38#2/r12.anchor: أى لا تفعل بى ما هو أمنيتهم من الاستهاة بى والإساءة إلى

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r1.claim: Ghaḍbān is diptote because its feminine is ghaḍbā and its alif and nūn function like the feminine alif; here it is an accusative circumstantial.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r1.anchor: لم ينصرف «غضبان» لأن مؤنثه غضبى، ولأن الألف والنون فيه بمنزلة ألفي التأنيث في قولك حمراء. وهو نصب على الحال.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r2.claim: Asafan means intense anger; Abū al-Dardāʾ says it is a degree beyond anger and more intense.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r2.anchor: و «أسفا» شديد الغضب. قال أبو الدرداء: الأسف منزلة وراء الغضب أشد من ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r3.claim: They explain that Moses returned saddened by what his people had done.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r3.anchor: ابن عباس والسدي: رجع حزينا من صنيع قومه.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r4.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says God had told Moses before he returned that the people had been tested by the calf, so Moses came back angry.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r4.anchor: وقال الطبري: أخبره الله عز وجل قبل رجوعه أنهم قد فتنوا بالعجل فلذلك رجع وهو غضبان.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r5.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says Moses was exceptionally prone to anger but quick to recover, balancing the two traits.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r5.anchor: ابن العربي: وكان موسى عليه السلام من أعظم الناس غضبا، لكنه كان سريع الفيئة فتلك بتلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r6.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r6.claim: Ibn al-Qāsim reports Mālik saying smoke rose from Moses' cap and his body hair stood beneath his cloak when he became angry.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r6.anchor: قال ابن القاسم: سمعت مالكا يقول: كان موسى عليه السلام إذا غضب طلع الدخان من قلنسوته

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r7.claim: Anger is like an ember burning in the heart; the Prophet instructed an angry person to lie down, and, if anger remained, to bathe, extinguishing it with rest and water.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r7.anchor: وذلك أن الغضب جمرة تتوقد في القلب. ولأجله أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من غضب أن يضطجع.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r8.claim: Moses' quick anger caused him to strike the Angel of Death and gouge out his eye, a matter previously discussed under al-Māʾidah.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r8.anchor: وسرعة غضبه كان سببا لصكه ملك الموت ففقأ عينه. وقد تقدم في «المائدة» ما للعلماء في هذا.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r9.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r9.claim: Al-Tirmidhī al-Ḥakīm says Moses was permitted to act because he was God's intimate interlocutor and anyone who reached toward him with harm had committed a grave offense.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r9.anchor: وقال الترمذي الحكيم: وإنما استجاز موسى عليه السلام ذلك لأنه كليم الله كأنه رأى أن من اجترأ عليه أو مد إليه يدا بأذى فقد عظم الخطب فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r10.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r10.claim: He recounts Moses challenging the Angel of Death: how could his soul be taken from the mouth that spoke privately with God, ears that heard God's speech, hands that received the tablets, feet on the mountain, or eyes illuminated by His light?
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r10.anchor: أمن فمي وقد ناجيت به ربي! أم من سمعي وقد سمعت به كلام ربي! أم من يدي وقد قبضت منه الألواح!

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r11.speaker: الترمذي الحكيم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r11.claim: After Moses' argument, the Angel of Death returned to his Lord unable to answer.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r12.speaker: أبو ذر
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r12.claim: A report in Abū Dāwūd's Muṣannaf from Abū Dharr says the Prophet advised an angry person who is standing to sit; if anger remains, to lie down. No grading is stated.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r12.anchor: وفي مصنف أبي داود عن أبي ذر قال: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لنا:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r13.speaker: أبو وائل القاص
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r13.claim: Abū Wāʾil recounts that ʿUrwa ibn Muḥammad became angry with a visitor, left, returned after ablution, and then reported a Prophetic teaching transmitted through his father and grandfather ʿAṭiyya.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151/r13.anchor: وروي أيضا عن أبي وائل القاص قال: دخلنا على عروة بن محمد السعدي فكلمه رجل فأغضبه فقام ثم رجع وقد توضأ

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r1.speaker: عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r1.claim: The Prophet said anger comes from Satan, who was created from fire, and fire is extinguished with water; an angry person should perform ablution. No grading is stated.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r1.anchor: إن الغضب من الشيطان وإن الشيطان خلق من النار وإنما تطفأ النار بالماء

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r2.claim: Moses' phrase condemns the people's bad conduct after his departure; khalafa can describe treating one's household or people well or badly in one's absence.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r2.anchor: بئس العمل عملتم بعدي. يقال: خلفه بما يكره. ويقال في الخير أيضا.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r3.speaker: author
