QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r3.claim: Aʿajiltum amra rabbikum means you got ahead of it; doing something before its appointed time is blameworthy, while doing it at the first proper time is praiseworthy.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r3.anchor: أي سبقتموه. والعجلة: التقدم بالشيء قبل وقته، وهي مذمومة. والسرعة: عمل الشيء في أول أوقاته، وهي محمودة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r4.speaker: يعقوب
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r4.claim: Yaʿqūb explains ʿajaltu al-shayʾ as getting ahead of it, while aʿjaltu al-rajul means making him hurry.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#2/r4.anchor: قال يعقوب: يقال عجلت الشيء سبقته. وأعجلت الرجل استعجلته، أي حملته على العجلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r1.claim: Amr rabbikum may mean God's appointment, the promise of forty nights.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r1.anchor: ومعنى «أمر ربكم» أي ميعاد ربكم، أي وعد أربعين ليلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r2.claim: Some interpret the phrase as having hastened your Lord's anger.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r3.claim: Some interpret it as worshipping the calf before a command from God had come to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r3.anchor: وقيل: أعجلتم بعبادة العجل قبل أن يأتيكم أمر من ربكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explains that Moses threw the tablets from anger and grief when he saw the people worshipping the calf and his brother had let matters go unmanaged; seeing is not like hearing.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r4.anchor: أي مما اعتراه من الغضب والأسف حين أشرف على قومه وهم عاكفون على عبادة العجل، وعلى أخيه في إهمال أمرهم قاله سعيد بن جبير.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r5.claim: He rejects as a bad, unworthy claim the report attributed to Qatāda that Moses threw the tablets after seeing the merit of Muhammad's community in them, a merit not given to his own community.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r5.anchor: ولا التفات لما روي عن قتادة إن صح عنه، ولا يصح: أن إلقاءه الألواح إنما كان لما رأى فيها من فضيلة أمة محمد

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r7.claim: He rejects the Sufi analogy between Moses' act and ecstatic musicians throwing or tearing clothes while claiming loss of awareness excuses them.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r7.anchor: وقد استدل بعض جهال المتصوفة بهذا على جواز رمي الثياب إذا اشتد طربهم على المغنى.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r8.speaker: أبو الفرج الجوزي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r8.claim: Ibn al-Jawzī asks who can authenticate that Moses threw the tablets as one who intended to break them: scripture only says he cast them down, and neither breakage nor intent is established.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r8.anchor: قال أبو الفرج الجوزي: من يصحح عن موسى عليه السلام أنه رماها رمي كاسر؟ والذي ذكر في القرآن ألقاها

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r9.speaker: أبو الفرج الجوزي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r9.claim: Even if the tablets broke, one cannot infer Moses meant to break them or claim he was unconscious; such an extreme hypothetical does not excuse people who knowingly attend music.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r9.anchor: ثم لو قيل: تكسرت فمن أين لنا أنه قصد كسرها؟ ثم لو صححنا ذلك عنه قلنا كان في غيبة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r10.speaker: أبو الفرج الجوزي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r10.claim: One cannot compare the states of prophets with those of foolish people.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r10.anchor: ثم كيف تقاس أحوال الأنبياء على أحوال هؤلاء السفهاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r11.speaker: ابن عقيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAqīl calls ecstatic behavior and tearing clothes wrong and forbidden, citing the Prophet's prohibition on wasting wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r11.anchor: وقد سئل ابن عقيل عن تواجدهم وتخريق ثيابهم فقال: خطأ وحرام وقد نهى رسول الله صلى الله

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r12.speaker: ابن عقيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r12.claim: Those who knowingly enter places where music overwhelms their reason are responsible for the resulting damage; legal duties remain because they were warned before entering.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r12.anchor: إن حضروا هذه الأمكنة مع علمهم أن الطرب يغلب عليهم فيزيل عقولهم أثموا بما أدخلوه على أنفسهم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r13.speaker: ابن عقيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r13.claim: If the claimed ecstasy is genuine, it is natural intoxication; if false, people act corruptly while sober, so neither account makes it safe and avoiding doubtful settings is obligatory.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#3/r13.anchor: كذلك هذا الطرب الذي يسميه أهل التصوف وجدا إن صدقوا أن فيه سكر طبع، وإن كذبوا أفسدوا مع الصحو

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r1.claim: The second view says Moses grasped Aaron to whisper about the tablets revealed during their private conversation and hide them from Israel.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r1.anchor: الثاني أن ذلك إنما كان ليسر إليه نزول الألواح عليه لأنها نزلت عليه في هذه المناجاة وأراد أن يخفيها عن بني إسرائيل

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r2.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r2.claim: The fourth view says Moses embraced Aaron to learn what had happened; Aaron feared Israel would mistake it for humiliation.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r2.anchor: الرابع ضم إليه أخاه ليعلم ما لديه فكره ذلك هارون لئلا يظن بنو إسرائيل أنه أهانه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r3.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r3.claim: A second interpretation says Moses wanted to whisper about the tablets revealed during the private conversation and conceal them from the Israelites; Aaron objected lest the gesture look humiliating.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r3.anchor: الثاني أن ذلك إنما كان ليسر إليه نزول الألواح عليه لأنها نزلت عليه في هذه المناجاة وأراد أن يخفيها عن بني إسرائيل

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r4.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r4.claim: A third interpretation is that Moses suspected Aaron sided with the calf-worshippers; Qurtubi says this suspicion is impermissible for prophets.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r4.anchor: الثالث إنما فعل ذلك به لأنه وقع في نفسه أن هارون مائل مع بني إسرائيل فيما فعلوه من أمر العجل. ومثل هذا لا يجوز على الأنبياء.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r5.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r5.claim: Aaron explained that the calf-worshippers had oppressed him and nearly killed him.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r5.anchor: فبين له أخوه أنهم استضعفوه، يعني عبدة العجل، وكادوا يقتلونه أي قاربوا.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r9.claim: Aaron's fear that the people would kill him shows that a person who fears being killed while forbidding wrong may remain silent.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r9.anchor: فبين هارون أنه إنما أقام خوفا على نفسه من القتل. فدلت الآية على أن لمن خشي القتل على نفسه عند تغيير المنكر أن يسكت.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r10.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r10.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says anger does not alter legal rulings as some claim: Moses' actions continued in their ordinary course despite his anger.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r10.anchor: ابن العربي: وفيها دليل على أن الغضب لا يغير الأحكام كما زعم بعض الناس فإن موسى عليه السلام لم يغير غضبه شيئا من أفعاله

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r11.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r11.claim: Al-Mahdawī says Moses' anger was for God, while he remained silent toward the Israelites from fear they would fight and divide.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r11.anchor: المهدوي: لأن غضبه كان لله عز وجل، وسكوته عن بني إسرائيل خوفا أن يتحاربوا ويتفرقوا.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r12.claim: Ibn um is a tender, affectionate form of address, even though Aaron was Moses' brother by both parents.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r12.anchor: وكان ابن أمه وأبيه. ولكنها كلمة لين وعطف.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r13.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r13.claim: Al-Zajjāj says it was reported that Aaron was Moses' maternal brother but not his paternal brother.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r13.anchor: قال الزجاج: قيل كان هارون أخا موسى لأمه لا لأبيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r14.claim: The vocative ibn um is read with the mīm open or kasra; with an open mīm, the words become one compound name like khamsata ʿashar.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r14.anchor: وقرىء بفتح الميم وكسرها فمن فتح جعل «ابن أم» اسما واحدا كخمسة عشر

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r15.claim: With a kasra, ibn um is possessive to the first-person pronoun; the yāʾ is omitted in vocative speech and its trace remains as the mīm's kasra.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r15.anchor: ومن كسر الميم جعله مضافا إلى ضمير المتكلم ثم حذف ياء الإضافة لأن مبنى النداء على الحذف

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r16.claim: The phrase ya ʿibādī at 39:10 is cited to support retaining a kasra as a sign of the omitted possessive yāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#4/r16.anchor: وأبقى الكسرة في الميم لتدل على الإضافة كقوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r1.speaker: ابن السميقع
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r1.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqiʿ reads yā-bna ummī, retaining the yāʾ of the original form.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r1.anchor: يدل عليه قراءة ابن السميقع «يابن أمي» بإثبات الياء على الأصل.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r2.speaker: الكسائي والفراء وأبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r2.claim: They read yā-bna um with an open mīm, analyzing it as yā-bna umāh.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r2.anchor: وقال الكسائي والفراء وأبو عبيد: «يابن أم» بالفتح، تقديره يابن أماه.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r3.speaker: البصريون
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r3.claim: The Basran grammarians reject that analysis: the light alif is not elided, so the two nouns must instead be compounded.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r3.anchor: وقال البصريون: هذا القول خطأ لأن الألف خفيفة لا تحذف ولكن جعل الاسمين اسما واحدا.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r4.speaker: الأخفش وأبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r4.claim: They read the mīm with kasra but call this dialect rare and the reading remote; they object that a noun built into another construct normally keeps its possessive suffix.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r4.anchor: وقال الأخفش وأبو حاتم: «يابن أم» بالكسر كما تقول: يا غلام غلام أقبل، وهي لغة شاذة والقراءة بها بعيدة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r5.speaker: الأخفش وأبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r5.claim: They allow ibn um and ibn ʿamm because those phrases are frequent in speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r5.anchor: وجوزوا يابن أم، يابن عم، لكثرتها في الكلام.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r6.speaker: الزجاج والنحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r6.claim: They offer a sound analysis: ibn with um or ʿamm forms one compound like khamsata ʿashar, and the possessive yāʾ is omitted as in yā ghulām.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج والنحاس: ولكن لها وجه حسن جيد، يجعل الابن مع الأم ومع العم اسما واحدا بمنزلة قولك: يا خمسة عشر

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r7.claim: Istadaʿafūnī means they treated me as weak and powerless; kādū means they nearly did it.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r7.anchor: { إن القوم استضعفوني } استذلوني وعدوني ضعيفا. { وكادوا } أي قاربوا.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r8.claim: The recited yaqtulūnanī has two nūns because it is a future verb, though assimilation is possible outside Qur'anic recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r8.anchor: { يقتلونني } بنونين لأنه فعل مستقبل. ويجوز الإدغام في غير القرآن.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r9.claim: Shamāta is rejoicing at a brother's religious or worldly misfortune; Moses asks that enemies not rejoice, and such gloating is forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r9.anchor: والشماتة: السرور بما يصيب أخاك من المصائب في الدين والدنيا. وهي محرمة منهي عنها.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r10.speaker: محمد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r10.claim: The Prophet forbade gloating over one's brother, warning that God might relieve him and test the one who gloats.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r10.anchor: وفي الحديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r11.speaker: محمد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r11.claim: The Prophet sought refuge from an evil decree, distress, and the gloating of enemies; Qurtubi says al-Bukhārī and others recorded it.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r11.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتعوذ منها ويقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r12.claim: A poem illustrates that people who gloat over another's hardship may later suffer the same fate.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r12.anchor: وقال الشاعر: إذا ما الدهر جر على أناس كلاكله أناخ بآخرينا

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r13.speaker: مجاهد ومالك بن دينار
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r13.claim: They read tushmit with the tāʾ in the subjunctive and al-aʿdāʾ nominative: do not do something to me that gives enemies cause to gloat.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r13.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد ومالك بن دينار «تشمت» بالنصب في التاء وفتح الميم، «الأعداء» بالرفع.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r14.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r14.claim: He also reads tushmit with open vowels and al-aʿdāʾ accusative; Ibn Jinnī explains this as Moses asking God not to make the enemies gloat over him.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r14.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا «تشمت» بالفتح فيهما «الأعداء» بالنصب. قال ابن جني: المعنى فلا تشمت بي أنت يا رب.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r15.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r15.claim: Abū ʿUbayd reports Ḥumayd's reading tushmit with kasra on the mīm.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r15.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: وحكيت عن حميد: «فلا تشمت» بكسر الميم.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r16.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r16.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says the kasra reading has no valid basis: the sh-m-t form would require tashmat, while the causative form would require tushemit.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r16.anchor: قال النحاس: ولا وجه لهذه القراءة لأنه إن كان من شمت وجب أن يقول تشمت. وإن كان من أشمت وجب أن يقول تشمت

QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r17.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r17.claim: Mujāhid interprets the wrongdoers Moses asks not to join as the people who worshipped the calf.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:150-151#5/r17.anchor: قال مجاهد: يعني الذين عبدوا العجل.

RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r1.claim: The verse neither rules out Moses knowing of the calf worship beforehand nor requires it; he could have learned on reaching the people.
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r1.anchor: لا يمنع من أن يكون قد عرف خبرهم من قبل في عبادة العجل ، / ولا يوجب ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r2.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r2.claim: Some say Moses discovered the calf worship only when he confronted the people on arriving.
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r2.anchor: فقال قوم : إنه عند هجومه عليهم عرف ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r3.claim: Abu Muslim says Moses already knew beforehand; al-Razi prefers this because the verse says he was angry while returning, before reaching them, and Ta Ha says God told him at the appointed meeting.
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم : بل كان عارفا بذلك من قبل ، وهذا أقرب ، ويدل عليه وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi’s first argument for prior knowledge is that Moses was already angry and grieving while still on his way, before reaching the people.
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى : { ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا } يدل على أنه حال ما كان راجعا

RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r5.claim: His second argument is that Ta Ha says God informed Moses of the event at the appointed meeting.
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r5.anchor: أنه تعالى ذكر في سورة طه أنه أخبره بوقوع تلك الواقعة في الميقات

RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r6.speaker: أبو الدرداء وعطاء عن ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak? No: Abu al-Darda and Ata, reporting from Ibn Abbas, define asaf as intense anger; al-Zajjaj chooses this sense, supported by 43:55.
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r6.anchor: أن الأسف الشديد الغضب ، وهو قول أبي الدرداء وعطاء ، عن ابن عباس واختيار الزجاج

RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والسدي
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and al-Suddi also interpret asaf as grief; Aisha described Abu Bakr as asif, meaning sorrowful.
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r7.anchor: وهو أيضا قول ابن عباس والحسن والسدي ، إن الآسف هو الحزين . وفي حديث عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت

RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r8.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r8.claim: Al-Wahidi says the anger and grief readings are close: what comes from an inferior provokes anger, while what comes from a superior brings grief.
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r8.anchor: قال الواحدي : والقولان متقاربان ، لأن الغضب من الحزن والحزن من الغضب

RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r9.claim: Al-Razi combines the senses: Moses was angry at the people for worshipping the calf and grieved that God had tested them.
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r9.anchor: فعلى هذا كان موسى غضبان على قومه لأجل عبادتهم العجل ، أسفا حزينا ، لأن الله تعالى فتنهم

RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r10.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r10.claim: One reading of bi’sama khalaftumuni addresses the calf worshippers, including al-Samiri and his followers: they badly succeeded Moses by replacing God’s worship with calf worship.
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r10.anchor: وهذا الخطاب إنما يكون لعبدة العجل من السامري وأشياعه

RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r11.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r11.claim: Another reading addresses Israel’s leaders, Aaron and the believers with him, for failing to stop worship of another besides God; 7:142 calls Moses’ deputy to succeed him among his people.
RAZI-FULL:v15p9#2/r11.anchor: أو لوجوه بني إسرائيل ، وهم : هارون عليه السلام والمؤمنون معه

RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r1.claim: In bi’sa, the subject is implicit and explained by ma khalaf; the item condemned is omitted and understood as their bad succession.
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r1.anchor: الفاعل مضمر يفسره قوله : { ما * خلفتمونى } والمخصوص بالذم محذوف تقديره

RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r2.claim: Min baʿdi means after Moses taught monotheism, rejected partners, and devoted worship to God; alternatively, after he had prevented Israel from worshipping the calf, as in 7:138. A deputy should follow the one who appointed him.
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r2.anchor: معناه من بعد ما رأيتم مني من توحيد الله تعالى ، ونفي الشركاء عنه وإخلاص العبادة له

RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r3.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r3.claim: Al-Wahidi distinguishes blameworthy ʿajala, doing something before its proper time, from non-blameworthy surʿa, doing it at the earliest proper time.
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r3.anchor: العجلة التقدم بالشيء قبل وقته / ولذلك صارت مذمومة / والسرعة غير مذمومة ، لأن معناها عمل الشيء في أول أوقاته

RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r4.claim: Al-Razi raises Moses’ statement that he hurried to God as an objection to treating haste as blameworthy, then records several readings of amr rabbikum.
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r4.anchor: لو كانت العجلة مذمومة ، فلم قال موسى عليه السلام : { وعجلت إليك رب لترضى }

RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reads amr rabbikum as God’s appointed meeting: why did you not wait for your Lord’s appointment?
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس المعنى : { أعجلتم أمر ربكم } يعني ميعاد ربكم فلم تصبروا له

RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r6.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r6.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the matter as the promised forty days: Israel assumed Moses had died when thirty days passed without his return.
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن : وعد ربكم الذي وعدكم من الأربعين ، وذلك لأنهم قدروا أنه لما لم يأت

RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r7.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r7.claim: Ata interprets the phrase as asking whether they hastened their Lord’s wrath.
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r7.anchor: وقال عطاء : يريد أعجلتم سخط ربكم

RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r8.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r8.claim: Al-Kalbi says they hastened by worshipping the calf before God’s command arrived.
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r8.anchor: وقال الكلبي : أعجلتم بعبادة العجل قبل أن يأتيكم أمر ربكم

RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r9.claim: Throwing the tablets, which bore the Torah and were Moses’ greatest miracle, signals overwhelming anger because a person would not do this otherwise.
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r9.anchor: يريد التي فيها التوراة ، ولما كانت تلك الألواح أعظم معاجزه ، ثم أنه ألقاها دل ذلك على شدة الغضب

RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r10.speaker: روي
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r10.claim: An unattributed report says the Torah had seven portions; the tablets broke, six portions were lifted, and one remained containing guidance and mercy while the lifted portions held detailed knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r10.anchor: فلما ألقى الألواح تكسرت ، فرفع منها ستة أسباعها وبقي سبع واحد

RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r11.claim: The Prophet says God have mercy on Moses: eyewitnessing the people’s trial was not like merely hearing of it, though Moses knew God’s warning was true and still held what was in his hand.
RAZI-FULL:v15p10/r11.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( يرحم الله أخي موسى ليس الخبر كالمعاينة

RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r1.claim: Al-Razi objects that the Qur’an only says Moses threw the tablets; claiming they broke lacks scriptural proof and is an audacious account unworthy of prophets.
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r1.anchor: ليس في القرآن إلا أنه ألقى الألواح فأما أنه ألقاها بحيث تكسرت ، فهذا ليس في القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r2.speaker: الطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r2.claim: Those who challenge prophetic impeccability say Moses pulled Aaron’s head toward him to humiliate and belittle him.
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r2.anchor: فالطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء يقولون إنه أخذ برأس أخيه يجره إليه على سبيل الإهانة والاستخفاف

RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r3.speaker: المثبتون لعصمة الأنبياء
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r3.claim: Those who affirm prophetic impeccability say Moses drew Aaron close in order to speak privately and learn what had happened.
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r3.anchor: والمثبتون لعصمة الأنبياء قالوا إنه جر رأس أخيه إلى نفسه ليساره ويستكشف منه كيفية تلك الواقعة

RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r4.claim: Aaron feared ignorant Israelites would think Moses was angry with him as with the calf worshippers; they had ignored Aaron’s warning and nearly killed him.
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r4.anchor: خاف أن يتوهم جهال بني إسرائيل أن موسى عليه السلام غضبان عليه كما أنه غضبان على عبدة العجل

RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r5.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r5.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, al-Kisa’i, and Abu Bakr from Asim read ibn ummi with kasra on the mīm here and in Ta Ha, deleting the possessive yā because vocatives commonly omit it; the kasra signals possession.
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم { ابن أم } / بكسر الميم ، وفي طه مثله

RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r6.speaker: الباقون
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r6.claim: The remaining readers use fatḥ on the mīm in both suras; one explanation treats ibn umm as a single compound name, like Hadramawt or fifteen.
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r6.anchor: والباقون بفتح الميم في السورتين ، وفيه قولان : أحدهما : أنهما جعلا اسما واحدا

RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r7.speaker: الباقون
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r7.claim: The other explanation drops the alif that replaces the possessive yā, giving the original yā-bna-ammā; an unnamed poet’s line beginning yā-bnata ʿammā illustrates it.
RAZI-FULL:v15p11/r7.anchor: وثانيهما : أنه على حذف الألف المبدلة من ياء الإضافة ، وأصله يا ابن أما كما قال الشاعر : يا ابنة عما

RAZI-FULL:v15p11#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p11#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p11#2/r1.claim: Aaron explains that the people disregarded him and nearly killed him; asking Moses not to gladden enemies means not to leave him sharing the calf worshippers’ punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v15p11#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { إن القوم استضعفوني } أي لم يلتفتوا إلى كلامي وكادوا يقتلونني ، فلا تشمت بي الأعداء

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r1.claim: Moses was already angry and aggrieved before seeing the people because God told him on the mountain that they had gone astray.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r1.anchor: Moses returned to his people already angry and aggrieved, even before seeing them, because God made him aware of their having gone astray while he was still on the mountain

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r2.claim: Asifan can mean sadness as well as intense anger.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r2.anchor: Aggrieved translates asifan, which may connote sadness, but also intense anger (Mw, Ṭ, Z).

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r3.claim: Some understand Moses’ anger as directed also at himself for leaving the people.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r3.anchor: but also perhaps at himself for having left them (Mw, Su),

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r4.claim: His grief may concern both the people’s grave error and his departure from intimate discourse with God.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r4.anchor: his grief was both for his people’s grave error and for his having to leave the intimate discourse with God (Mw, Su)

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r5.claim: Moses’ complaint about the evil course may address all Israelites or their leaders, including Aaron.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r5.anchor: may have been directed at the Israelites generally or at the leaders among them, including Aaron (Z);

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r6.claim: “After me” may mean while Moses was away or after he had set an example of true monotheism.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r6.anchor: after me may mean while Moses was away (IK, Ṭ, Ṭs) or after Moses had set the example of true monotheism (R, Z).

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r7.claim: The Command may refer to waiting for Moses’ return; the people were impatient and hastened his return.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r7.anchor: the command that they wait for Moses’ return. It thus addresses their impatience concerning—and their ultimate hastening of—Moses’ return

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r8.claim: Moses’ forty-day stay reportedly lasted ten days beyond what the people expected.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r8.anchor: Moses’ forty-day stay upon the mountain was reportedly ten days longer than his people had expected.

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r9.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r9.claim: The Command may refer to the people hastening God’s judgment through their actions, a Quranic warning to disbelievers.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r9.anchor: It may also refer to their hastening God’s judgment upon them through their actions (R), a repeated Quranic warning to disbelievers

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r10.claim: More broadly, Moses may chastise their impatience about God fulfilling His promise, as he does in the parallel account.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r10.anchor: More broadly, the question might also be meant to chastise them for their impatience regarding God’s fulfillment of His Promise to them

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r11.claim: Moses cast down the Tablets in anger and shock, breaking them, as in the Biblical account.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r11.anchor: Moses throws down the Tablets in anger (Ṭ) and shock (Z) upon seeing his people’s idolatrous worship, breaking them (R, Ṭ, Z), as in the Biblical account

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r12.claim: Moses seized Aaron in anger because Aaron had failed to preserve the Israelites in righteousness.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r12.anchor: He then seizes his brother, Aaron, in anger for his having failed in his charge of preserving the Israelites in righteousness

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r13.claim: The Quran gives another account of Moses’ confrontation with Aaron.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r13.anchor: For another narrative of Moses’ confrontation with Aaron, see 20:92–94.

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r14.claim: Aaron says “son of my mother” rather than simply brother to evoke Moses’ tenderness and mercy.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r14.anchor: calling him son of my mother, rather than just “my brother,”in a bid to evoke Moses’ tenderness and mercy toward him

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r15.claim: Aaron says the people deemed him weak, meaning they no longer recognized his authority, as shown by their following al-Sāmirī and ignoring his pleas.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r15.anchor: meaning that they no longer recognized his authority (R, Ṭ)—as suggested by their having followed instead the directives of al-Sāmirī

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r16.claim: Aaron says the people were prepared to kill him; elsewhere he explains that stronger action might have made him blamed for causing discord.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r16.anchor: and were moreover prepared to slay him; see also 20:94, where Aaron argues that he feared he would be blamed for causing discord among the Israelites

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r17.claim: Aaron asks Moses not to let enemies gloat over his further humiliation at Moses’ hands.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r17.anchor: not to let their enemies rejoice in his misfortune—that is, to gloat over his further humiliation at the hands of Moses

STUDYQURAN:7:150/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r18.claim: Aaron asks not to be classed with wrongdoers, meaning not to be judged guilty of idolatry and punished with the others.
STUDYQURAN:7:150/r18.anchor: not to place him with the wrongdoing people, that is, not to consider him guilty of idolatry and so punish him along with the others

SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r1.claim: غضبان and أسفا may both be circumstantial predicates of Moses; if multiple circumstantials are disallowed, أسفا can modify the implicit pronoun inside غضبان.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r1.anchor: حالان من موسى عند من يجيز تعدد الحال، وعند من لا يجيزه يجعل

SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r2.claim: Alternatively أسفا is apposition to غضبان: partitive if it means intensely angry, or apposition of inclusion if it means grieved; their closeness makes this possible.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r2.anchor: وفيه نظر لعسر إدخاله في أقسام البدل، وأقرب ما يقال: إنه بدل بعض من كل

SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r3.claim: أسف can mean that anger intensified, as in the Qurʾanic usage in 43:55.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r3.anchor: يقال: أسف يأسف أسفا، أي: اشتد غضبه. قال تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r4.claim: أسف can also mean grief; a poem describing a time passing in sorrow illustrates the meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r4.anchor: ويقال: بل معناه حزن ومنه قوله:

SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r5.speaker: الواحدي
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r5.claim: Al-Wāḥidī cites a verse associating a grieving person with an angry person, evidence that the two senses are close.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r5.anchor: ما بينهما كما قال الواحدي قوله:

SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r6.claim: Al-Aʿshā's description of a man as أسيف uses the word in the sense of angry.

SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r7.claim: A hadith calls Abū Bakr a man أسيف, meaning grieved.

SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r8.claim: أسف describes an established, settled quality, while أسف on the فاعل pattern is used for a temporary state.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150/r8.anchor: ورجل أسف: إذا قصد ثبوت الوصف واستقراره، فإن قصد به الزمان جاء على فاعل.

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#2/r1.claim: بئسما answers لما; its condemned object is omitted, and the hidden subject is explained by ما خلفتموني, meaning your succession was a bad one.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#2/r1.anchor: هذا جواب " لما " وتقدم الكلام على " بئسما " ، ولكن المخصوص بالذم محذوف،

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses أمر as an object after dropping عن: عجل عن الأمر means leaving it unfinished, and the verb can take a direct object with the sense of سبق.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#2/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " يقال: عجل عن الأمر: إذا تركه غير تام، ونقيضه تم،

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#2/r3.speaker: يعقوب
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#2/r3.claim: Yaʿqūb allows direct transitivity without supplying another verb's sense: عجلت الشيء means I preceded it, while أعجلت الرجل means I made him hurry.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#2/r3.anchor: حكى يعقوب " عجلت الشيء سبقته " وأعجلت الرجل استعجلته، أي: حملته على العجلة ".

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r1.claim: يجره إليه can be circumstantial for Moses, the hidden subject of أخذ: he took him while dragging him toward himself.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r1.anchor: أحدها: أن الجملة حال من ضمير موسى المستتر في " أخذ " ، أي: أخذ جارا إليه.

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ proposes that the clause modifies رأس, but the author objects that this reading lacks a linking pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r2.anchor: الثاني: أنها حال من " رأس " قاله أبو البقاء وفيه نظر لعدم الرابط.

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r3.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also attaches the circumstantial clause to أخيه; the author calls it weak because a circumstantial clause from a genitive possessor is rare or disallowed, though some permit it when the possessor's part is meant.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r3.anchor: الثالث: أنها حال من " أخيه " قال أبو البقاء: " وهو ضعيف يعني من حيث/ إن الحال من المضاف إليه

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r4.claim: The author accepts the genitive-possessor construction in cases where the possessed noun is a part of its possessor.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r4.anchor: قلت: وقد تقدم غير مرة أن بعضهم يجوزه في صور هذه منها، وهو كون المضاف جزءا

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r5.speaker: الأخوان وأبو بكر وابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r5.claim: Al-Akhawān, Abū Bakr, and Ibn ʿĀmir read ابن أم with a kasra here and in Ṭā Hā; the others read it with a fatḥa.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r5.anchor: قرأ الأخوان وأبو بكر وابن عامر هنا وفي طه بكسر الميم والباقون بفتحها.

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r6.speaker: البصريون
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r6.claim: On the Basran account of the fatḥa reading, ابن أم is a compound like خمسة عشر, built on fatḥa rather than an iḍāfa construction.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r6.anchor: مذهب البصريين أنهما بنيا على الفتح لتركبهما تركيب خمسة عشر، فعلى هذا فليس

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r7.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r7.claim: The Kufans treat ابن as annexed to أم, itself annexed to the first-person yāʾ; yāʾ becomes alif and is deleted, with fatḥa substituting for it, so ابن is inflected and أم is genitive.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r7.anchor: والثاني: مذهب الكوفيين وهو أن " ابن " مضاف ل " أم " و " أم " مضافة لياء

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r8.speaker: البصريون
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r8.claim: For the kasra reading, Basrans treat the whole compound as annexed to the speaker's yāʾ, built with kasra as its substitute; they reject an ordinary iḍāfa because this genitive complement is not a vocative from which yāʾ may be dropped.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r8.anchor: وأما قراءة الكسر فعلى رأي البصريين هو كسر بناء لأجل ياء المتكلم، بمعنى أنا أضفنا

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r9.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r9.claim: For the kasra reading, Kufans take the kasra as inflection, with the deleted yāʾ represented by kasra, analogously to fatḥa representing a deleted alif.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r9.anchor: وعلى رأي الكوفيين يكون الكسر كسر إعراب وحذفت الياء مجتزأ عنها بالكسرة

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r10.claim: The four expressions ابن أم, ابن عم, ابنة أم, and ابنة عم have five licensed forms: delete yāʾ with kasra, change it to alif, delete alif with fatḥa, or retain yāʾ sākin or vocalized; their exceptional treatment reflects frequent use and treating the pair as one word.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#3/r10.anchor: فاعلم أنه يجوز في هذه الأمثلة الأربعة خاصة خمس لغات، فصحاهن: حذف الياء مجتزأ عنها بالكسرة،

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r1.claim: A reading retains the yāʾ in ابن أمي as sākin; two poetic examples illustrate it.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r1.anchor: وقرئ " يابن أمي " بإثبات الياء ساكنة، ومثله قوله:

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r2.claim: Another reading has ابن إم with kasra on both hamza and mīm by phonetic assimilation.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r2.anchor: وقرئ أيضا: " ابن إم " بكسر الهمزة والميم وهو إتباع.

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r3.claim: A poetic example such as كن لي لا علي يا بن عما shows yāʾ changing to alif.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r3.anchor: كن لي لا علي يا بن عما

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r4.claim: The standard reading has damma on ت and kasra on م in تشمت, from the quadriliteral أشمت, with الأعداء as its object.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r4.anchor: العامة على ضم التاء وكسر الميم وهو من أشمت رباعيا، " الأعداء " مفعول به.

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r5.speaker: ابن محيصن ومجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r5.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads تشمت with fatḥa on ت and kasra on م; Mujāhid has fatḥa on both, and both take الأعداء as object.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن " فلا تشمت " بفتح التاء وكسر الميم، ومجاهد بفتح التاء أيضا وفتح الميم،

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r6.claim: The clearest analysis makes the triliteral تشمت itself transitive like أشمت; this needs no implied subject or object.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r6.anchor: أظهرهما: أن شمت أو شمت بكسر الميم أو فتحها متعد بنفسه كأشمت الرباعي،

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r7.speaker: ابن جني
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r7.claim: Ibn Jinnī suggests that تشمت is addressed to God, with an implied object for الأعداء; the author rejects this as needless, since the triliteral verb is already transitive.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r7.anchor: قاله ابن جني، ولا حاجة إلى هذا التكلف لأن " شمت " الثلاثي يكون متعديا بنفسه،

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r8.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ reads the implied subject in the alternative parse as Moses himself, which the author says is preferable to making God the subject.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r8.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء في هذا التخريج : " فلا تشمت أنت " فجعل الفاعل ضمير موسى، وهو أولى

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r9.claim: The analogy with God mocking or scheming is valid only as a rhetorical counter to the opponents' mockery or scheming; such countering is absent here.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r9.anchor: ولا يجوز ذلك في غير المقابلة.

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r10.speaker: حميد بن قيس ومجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r10.claim: Ḥumayd ibn Qays and Mujāhid read the verb intransitively with الأعداء nominative as its subject; the prohibition formally addresses Moses while meaning he should not cause their gloating.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#4/r10.anchor: إلا أنهما رفعا الأعداء على الفاعلية، جعلا شمت/ لازما فرفعا به " الأعداء " على الفاعلية،

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r1.claim: Al-ishmāt and شماتة mean delight in a misfortune that befalls one's enemy; a poem says death is preferable to enemies' gloating.

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r2.claim: An etymology relates شماتة to an animal's legs, because a gloating heart shifts between joy and grief as an animal's legs shift.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r2.anchor: قيل: واشتقاقها من شوامت الدابة وهي قوائمها؛ لأن الشماتة تقلب قلب الحاسد

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r3.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says the form with shīn is the more elevated of the two ways of saying a prayer for a sneezer.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: " الشين أعلى اللغتين "

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r4.speaker: ثعلب
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r4.claim: Thaʿlab says the original is the form with sīn, from samt, meaning direction and guidance.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r4.anchor: وقال ثعلب: " الأصل فيهما السين من السمت، وهو القصد والهدي ".

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r5.claim: One explanation of the shīn form of the sneezer's prayer is a wish that God steady the sneezer as an animal's legs are steady.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r5.anchor: وقيل: معنى تشميت العاطس بالمعجمة أن يثبته الله كما يثبت قوائم الدابة.

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r6.claim: Another explanation treats the intensive form as privative: may God remove gloating from the sneezer; with sīn it means restoring him to his former condition after his disturbance.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r6.anchor: وقيل: بل التفعيل للسلب، أي: أزال الله الشماتة به، وبالسين المهملة، أي: رده الله

SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r7.speaker: أبو بكر
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r7.claim: Abū Bakr records the usages سمته and سمت عليه, including the hadith wording وسمت عليهما.
SAMIN-DURR:7:150#5/r7.anchor: وقال أبو بكر: " يقال: سمته وسمت عليه، وفي الحديث:

TAB-FULL:v10p449/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r1.claim: Moses returned angry and grieved because God had told him his people were being tested and the Samaritan had led them astray.
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r1.anchor: لأن الله كان قد أخبره أنه قد فتن قومه، وأن السامري قد أضلهم

TAB-FULL:v10p449/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī defines asaf as intense anger and vexation toward the one who angered him.
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r2.anchor: والأسف: شدة الغضب والتغيظ به على من أغضبه

TAB-FULL:v10p449/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r3.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ says asaf is a degree beyond anger, more intense than anger itself.
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r3.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء: قول الله: " {غضبان أسفا} [الأعراف: 150] قال: الأسف: منزلة وراء الغضب أشد من ذلك

TAB-FULL:v10p449/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says asaf here means sad, while in 43:55 “when they angered Us” means they angered God; asaf can signify either anger or grief.
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا} [الأعراف: 150] يقول: أسفا حزينا وقال في الزخرف

TAB-FULL:v10p449/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses Moses’ state as both angry and grieving.
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r6.anchor: سمعت الحسن، يقول في قوله: " ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا قال: غضبان حزينا "

TAB-FULL:v10p449/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r7.claim: Moses calls their conduct after his departure a bad failure to carry out what he had entrusted to them concerning his people and their religion.
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r7.anchor: بئس الفعل فعلتم بعد فراقي إياكم وأوليتموني فيمن خلفت من ورائي من قومي فيكم وديني

TAB-FULL:v10p449/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r8.claim: The verb khalafahu can mean that someone leaves good or evil in the care of people or family after departing.
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r8.anchor: يقال منه: خلفه بخير وخلفه بشر إذا أولاه في أهله أو قومه

TAB-FULL:v10p449/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r9.claim: Moses asks whether they preempted God’s command for themselves and abandoned it; ʿajila means to precede or surpass, while aʿjalathu can mean to urge someone on.
TAB-FULL:v10p449/r9.anchor: أسبقتم أمر ربكم في نفوسكم، وذهبتم عنه؟ يقال منه: عجل فلان هذا الأمر: إذا سبقه

TAB-FULL:v10p452/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Moses’ anger at the calf worshippers led him to seize Aaron and throw down the tablets.
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: " {ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا} [الأعراف: 150] فأخذ برأس أخيه يجره إليه، وألقى الألواح من الغضب "

TAB-FULL:v10p452/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses pulled Aaron by the head and threw down the tablets out of anger.
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r2.anchor: عن القاسم بن أبي أيوب، قال: ثني سعيد بن جبير، قال: قال ابن عباس: " {ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا} [الأعراف: 150] فأخذ برأس أخيه

TAB-FULL:v10p452/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Moses heard idle voices, saw the people gathered around the calf, broke the tablets, and seized Aaron by the head.
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما رجع موسى إلى قومه، وكان قريبا منهم، سمع أصواتهم

TAB-FULL:v10p452/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r4.claim: Al-Suddī connects the episode to Moses’ speech in 20:86–87 and says Moses threw the tablets and seized Aaron by the head.
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r4.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " أخذ موسى الألواح ثم رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا

TAB-FULL:v10p452/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r5.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Moses saw the calf worship, dropped the tablets, and grabbed Aaron by the head and beard, invoking 20:93.
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r5.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قالا: " لما انتهى موسى إلى قومه فرأى ما هم عليه من عبادة العجل

TAB-FULL:v10p452/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r6.claim: Another view says Moses threw the tablets because he found virtues written in them for a different people, which grieved him.
TAB-FULL:v10p452/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: إنما ألقى موسى الألواح لفضائل أصابها فيها لغير قومه، فاشتد ذلك عليه

TAB-FULL:v10p453/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r1.claim: Qatāda’s report describes Ahmad’s community as the best community, commanding right and forbidding wrong; Moses asks that they be his community.
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {أخذ الألواح} [الأعراف: 154] قال: رب إني أجد في الألواح أمة، خير أمة أخرجت للناس

TAB-FULL:v10p453/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r2.claim: Qatāda says the community is last in creation but first to enter Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r2.anchor: رب إني أجد في الألواح أمة هم الآخرون السابقون: أي: آخرون في الخلق، سابقون في دخول الجنة

TAB-FULL:v10p453/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r3.claim: Qatāda reports that Ahmad’s community has its scriptures in its hearts and preserves them, unlike earlier communities whose books were read only by sight.
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r3.anchor: رب إني أجد في الألواح أمة أناجيلهم في صدورهم يقرءونها، وكان من قبلهم يقرءون كتابهم نظرا

TAB-FULL:v10p453/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r4.claim: Qatāda says they believe in the earlier and later Books and fight the paths of misguidance until they confront the lying Antichrist.
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r4.anchor: رب إني أجد في الألواح أمة يؤمنون بالكتاب الأول وبالكتاب الآخر، ويقاتلون فصول الضلالة

TAB-FULL:v10p453/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r5.claim: Qatāda says their charity is consumed by its recipients and still earns reward, whereas accepted charity from earlier peoples was burned by fire.
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r5.anchor: رب إني أجد في الألواح أمة صدقاتهم يأكلونها في بطونهم ثم يؤجرون عليها

TAB-FULL:v10p453/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r6.claim: Qatāda reports that intending a good deed earns one reward even without acting; doing it earns tenfold up to seven hundredfold.
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r6.anchor: رب إني أجد في الألواح أمة إذا هم أحدهم بحسنة ثم لم يعملها كتبت له حسنة

TAB-FULL:v10p453/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r7.claim: Qatāda says an intended sin is not recorded until done, and then is recorded as one sin.
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r7.anchor: رب إني أجد في الألواح أمة إذا هم أحدهم بسيئة لم تكتب عليه حتى يعملها

TAB-FULL:v10p453/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r8.claim: Qatāda also describes the community as people whose prayers are answered and who intercede for others and receive intercession.
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r8.anchor: رب إني أجد في الألواح أمة هم المستجيبون والمستجاب لهم

TAB-FULL:v10p453/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r9.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r9.claim: Qatāda reports that Moses asked to be made part of Ahmad’s community and cast down the tablets; God then granted him prophethood’s distinction and a guided, just community among his people.
TAB-FULL:v10p453/r9.anchor: وذكر لنا أن نبي الله موسى عليه السلام نبذ الألواح وقال: اللهم اجعلني من أمة أحمد

TAB-FULL:v10p455/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r1.claim: Qatāda retells Moses’ wish to join Ahmad’s community after finding its virtues on the tablets, followed by his casting them down.
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r1.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة، قال: " لما أخذ موسى الألواح، قال: يا رب إني أجد في الألواح أمة هم خير الأمم

TAB-FULL:v10p455/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that Moses threw the tablets out of anger at calf worship, because the Qur’an explicitly links their throwing to his anger.
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r2.anchor: والذي هو أولى بالصواب من القول في ذلك أن يكون سبب إلقاء موسى الألواح كان من أجل غضبه

TAB-FULL:v10p455/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r3.claim: ʿAlī reports that God wrote the tablets for Moses while Moses heard the scratching of the pens.
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r3.anchor: عن السدي، عن أبي عمارة، عن علي، عليه السلام قال: «كتب الله الألواح لموسى عليه السلام وهو يسمع صريف الأقلام في الألواح»

TAB-FULL:v10p455/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Moses was brought near until he heard the scratching of the pens.
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: «أدناه حتى سمع صريف الأقلام»

TAB-FULL:v10p455/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r5.claim: A report says the Torah had seven parts; when Moses threw the tablets and they broke, six sevenths containing detailed instruction were lifted, leaving guidance and mercy in the remaining seventh.
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r5.anchor: وقيل: إن التوراة كانت سبعة أسباع فلما ألقى موسى الألواح تكسرت، فرفع منها ستة أسباعها

TAB-FULL:v10p455/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r6.claim: The Torah is also said to have been seventy camel-loads, with one portion read each year.
TAB-FULL:v10p455/r6.anchor: وكانت التوراة فيما ذكر سبعين وقر بعير يقرأ منها الجزء في سنة

TAB-FULL:v10p456/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r1.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r1.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas says the Torah was seventy camel-loads, one portion was read yearly, and only Moses, Jesus, Ezra, and Joshua read it.
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r1.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس، قال: " أنزلت التوراة وهي سبعون وقر بعير، يقرأ منها الجزء في سنة

TAB-FULL:v10p456/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r2.claim: One reported view says the tablets were made of green emerald.
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r2.anchor: واختلفوا في الألواح، فقال بعضهم: كانت من زمرد أخضر.

TAB-FULL:v10p456/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r3.claim: Another reported view says the tablets were made of ruby.

TAB-FULL:v10p456/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r4.claim: A further reported view says the tablets were made of bard (a cold or hail-like material).

TAB-FULL:v10p456/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the tablets broke when Moses threw them and all but one sixth was lifted away.
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " ألقى موسى الألواح فتكسرت، فرفعت إلا سدسها.

TAB-FULL:v10p456/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that the tablets were made of beryl and emerald from Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r6.anchor: قال ابن جريج: وأخبرني أن الألواح من زبرجد وزمرد من الجنة

TAB-FULL:v10p456/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r7.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says Moses’ tablets were made of bard.
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r7.anchor: عن أبي العالية، قال: «كانت ألواح موسى عليه السلام من برد»

TAB-FULL:v10p456/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r8.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the tablets were sapphire, their writing was gold, the Merciful wrote them by hand, and heaven heard the pen’s scratching.
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r8.anchor: سألت سعيد بن جبير عن الألواح، من أي شيء كانت؟ قال: «كانت من ياقوتة، كتابة الذهب

TAB-FULL:v10p456/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r9.speaker: مجاهد أو سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r9.claim: A report attributed uncertainly to Mujāhid or Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the tablets were emerald; after they were thrown, guidance and mercy remained while the detailed rulings were lost.
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد، أو سعيد بن جبير قال: «كانت الألواح زمردا، فلما ألقى موسى الألواح بقي الهدى والرحمة

TAB-FULL:v10p456/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r10.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r10.claim: Mujāhid separately says the tablets were green emerald.
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: «كانت الألواح من زمرد أخضر»

TAB-FULL:v10p456/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r11.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r11.claim: Some say there were two tablets; on that view, the plural “tablets” is still used just as “siblings” can denote two brothers.
TAB-FULL:v10p456/r11.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الألواح كانت لوحين، فإن كان الذي قال كما قال، فإنه قيل: {وكتبنا له في الألواح}

TAB-FULL:v10p457/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r1.claim: Moses seized Aaron because he was angry that Aaron had failed to follow him and had remained with the Israelites; after Aaron explained his fear of splitting the people, Moses accepted the excuse.
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r1.anchor: حين أخبره هارون بعذره، فقبل عذره، وذلك قيله لموسى

TAB-FULL:v10p457/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r2.speaker: قراء المدينة وبعض أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r2.claim: Most Medinan readers and some Basrans read ابن أم with an open mīm.
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r2.anchor: قرأ ذلك عامة قراء المدينة وبعض أهل البصرة: {يا ابن أم} [طه: 94] بفتح الميم

TAB-FULL:v10p457/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r3.speaker: قراء الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r3.claim: Most Kufan readers read ابن أم with a kasra on the mīm.
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r3.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء أهل الكوفة: (يا ابن أم) بكسر الميم من الأم

TAB-FULL:v10p457/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r4.speaker: نحويّو البصرة
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r4.claim: Basran grammarians say the open form combines two nouns as one name, like ibn ʿamm, though this is exceptional and not a productive pattern; the kasra follows another fused-name dialect.
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r4.anchor: قيل ذلك بالفتح على أنهما اسمان جعلا اسما واحدا، كما قيل: يا ابن عم، وقال: هذا شاذ لا يقاس عليه

TAB-FULL:v10p457/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r5.speaker: نحويّو الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r5.claim: Kufan grammarians explain the open ending as a vocative accusative like يا حسرتا, and the kasra as deletion of the first-person yāʾ in a frequent kinship vocative.
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r5.anchor: قيل: يا ابن أم ويا ابن عم، فنصب كما ينصب المعرب في بعض الحالات، فيقال: يا حسرتا، يا ويلتا

TAB-FULL:v10p457/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the open form means “son of my mother” as a lamenting vocative; the kasra is an annexation with the first-person yāʾ omitted.
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r6.anchor: فمراد به الندبة: يا ابن أماه، وكذلك من ابن عم فإذا كسرت فمراد به الإضافة

TAB-FULL:v10p457/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r7.speaker: بعض من أنكر نسبته ويونس النحوي
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r7.claim: Some explain the kasra by analogy with the paired expression khāz bāz; Yūnus says umm and ʿamm are feminine and form a single name only with masculine ibn.
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r7.anchor: وكأن بعض من أنكر نسبته كسر ذلك إذا كسر، ككسر الزاي من خاز باز

TAB-FULL:v10p457/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r8.claim: The soundest and most regular Arabic is يا ابن أمي with the yāʾ retained, as shown by Abū Zubayd’s poetry.
TAB-FULL:v10p457/r8.anchor: وأما اللغة الجيدة والقياس الصحيح فلغة من قال: «يا ابن أمي» بإثبات الياء، كما قال أبو زبيد:

TAB-FULL:v10p459/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r1.speaker: أبو زبيد
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r1.claim: Abū Zubayd’s line يا ابن أمي ويا شقيق نفسي is cited as poetic evidence for retaining the first-person yāʾ.
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r1.anchor: يا ابن أمي ويا شقيق نفسي … أنت خلفتني لدهر شديد

TAB-FULL:v10p459/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r2.speaker: شاعر آخر
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r2.claim: Another poet similarly uses يا ابن أمي with the yāʾ retained.
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r2.anchor: يا ابن أمي ولو شهدتك إذ تد … عو تميما وأنت غير مجاب

TAB-FULL:v10p459/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r3.claim: The yāʾ remains because the mother is not the vocative; the person called is the son, and Arabs drop yāʾ when the vocative adds the speaker to himself, not to someone else.
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r3.anchor: وإنما أثبت هؤلاء الياء في الأم؛ لأنها غير مناداة، وإنما المنادى هو الابن دونها

TAB-FULL:v10p459/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r4.claim: Although Moses and Aaron shared both parents, Aaron says “son of my mother” to appeal to Moses through their maternal bond.
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r4.anchor: وهما لأب واحد وأم واحدة، استعطافا له على نفسه برحم الأم

TAB-FULL:v10p459/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r5.claim: The people who weakened Aaron were the calf worshippers who claimed it was their god and Moses’ god and opposed Aaron.
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r5.anchor: يعني بالقوم الذين عكفوا على عبادة العجل، وقالوا هذا إلهنا وإله موسى، وخالفوا هارون

TAB-FULL:v10p459/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r6.claim: Their weakening of Aaron consisted of refusing to obey and follow his command.
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r6.anchor: وكان استضعافهم إياه، تركهم طاعته واتباع أمره

TAB-FULL:v10p459/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r7.claim: “They almost killed me” means they came close to killing Aaron but did not do so.

TAB-FULL:v10p459/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r8.speaker: قراء الأمصار
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r8.claim: The regional readers read tushmit with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the mīm, from the causative verb meaning to make someone rejoice at another’s misfortune.
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r8.anchor: قرأ قراء الأمصار ذلك: {فلا تشمت بي الأعداء} [الأعراف: 150] بضم التاء من تشمت وكسر الميم

TAB-FULL:v10p459/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r9.claim: Mujāhid is reported to read an alternate vocalization of تشمت; al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī allow it as a genuine Arabic variant with parallels in other verbs.
TAB-FULL:v10p459/r9.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد أنه قرأ ذلك: {فلا تشمت بي الأعداء} [الأعراف: 150]

TAB-FULL:v10p461/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p461/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p461/r1.claim: He accepts the reading fa-lā tushmit, vocalizing the first tāʾ with ḍamma and mīm with kasra; he reads al-aʿdāʾ in the accusative, following the readers' consensus and rejecting the anomalous alternative.
TAB-FULL:v10p461/r1.anchor: من قرأ: {فلا تشمت} [الأعراف: 150] بضم التاء الأولى وكسر الميم

TAB-FULL:v10p461/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p461/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p461/r2.claim: He says ordinary Arabic describes gloating over someone's enemy with shamita bihi, not the alternative construction he rejects.
TAB-FULL:v10p461/r2.anchor: وإنما المعروف من كلامهم إذا أخبروا عن شماتة الرجل بعدوه شمت به بكسر الميم يشمت به بفتحها في الاستقبال

TAB-FULL:v10p462/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p462/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p462/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the unjust people Harun means as the calf worshippers.
TAB-FULL:v10p462/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {ولا تجعلني مع القوم الظالمين} [الأعراف: 150] قال: أصحاب العجل "

TABATABAI:7:149-150/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r3.claim: Asaf means intense anger and grief; khilafa is taking up a predecessor's responsibility, and ʿajala means seeking something before its proper time, following al-Raghib's definition.
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r3.anchor: الأسف بكسر السين صفة مشبهة من الأسف وهو شدة الغضب والحزن والخلافة القيام بالأمر بعد غيره

TABATABAI:7:149-150/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r4.claim: Moses returned angry after God told him that his people had gone astray; he reproached them for badly succeeding him and hastening their Lord's affair.
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r4.anchor: ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه وهو في حال غضب وأسف لما أخبره الله تعالى لدى الرجوع بأن قومه ضلوا

TABATABAI:7:149-150/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r5.claim: The preferred reading is that they sought prematurely the Lord's promised affair at Moses' appointment, namely the Torah's descent; God's wise plan is unaffected by human haste or demand.
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بأمر ربهم أمره الذي لاجله واعد موسى لميقاته، وهو نزول التوراة

TABATABAI:7:149-150/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r6.claim: One alternative reads the rebuke as asking whether they worshipped the calf before a command from their Lord arrived.
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r6.anchor: وربما قيل إن معنى { أعجلتم أمر ربكم } أعجلتم بعبادة العجل قبل أن يأتيكم أمر من ربكم

TABATABAI:7:149-150/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r7.claim: Another alternative says they expected God's reward for worship, and turned to another object of worship when it did not arrive.
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r7.anchor: وقيل المعنى استعجلتم وعد الله وثوابه على عبادته فلما لم تنالوه عدلتم إلى عبادة غيره

TABATABAI:7:149-150/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r8.claim: A third alternative says they presumed Moses' appointment had ended and changed their practice rather than waiting for his return as God commanded.
TABATABAI:7:149-150/r8.anchor: وقيل المعنى أعجلتم عما أمركم به ربكم وهو انتظار رجوع موسى حافظين لعهده

TABATABAI:7:150/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:150/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:150/r1.claim: Moses threw down the Torah tablets and seized Aaron by the head, dragging him toward himself; Ta-Ha recounts Moses asking why Aaron did not follow the people when they strayed.
TABATABAI:7:150/r1.anchor: وكذا ما فعله موسى بأخيه من أخذ رأسه يجره إليه كأنه مقدمة لضربه

TABATABAI:7:150/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:150/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:150/r2.claim: Aaron's address 'son of my mother' instead of 'brother' or 'son of my father' softens Moses and stirs his compassion.
TABATABAI:7:150/r2.anchor: وإنما خاطبه بذكر أمهما دون أن يقول يا أخي أو يا ابن أبي للترقيق وتهييج الرحمة

TABATABAI:7:150/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:150/r3.speaker: هارون
TABATABAI:7:150/r3.claim: Aaron says the people overpowered him and nearly killed him because he opposed their calf worship; he asks Moses not to let enemies gloat or count him among wrongdoers.
TABATABAI:7:150/r3.anchor: إن القوم استضعفوني وكادوا يقتلونني } لما خالفتهم في أمر العجل ومنعتهم عن عبادته

TABATABAI:7:150/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:150/r4.speaker: هارون
TABATABAI:7:150/r4.claim: Aaron explains in Ta-Ha that he feared Moses would accuse him of dividing the Israelites and disregarding his instruction.
TABATABAI:7:150/r4.anchor: إني خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي

TABATABAI:7:150/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:150/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:150/r5.claim: The context indicates Moses was angry at Aaron too, believing he had not resisted the Israelites enough, though Aaron had judged restraint better for communal welfare.
TABATABAI:7:150/r5.anchor: وظاهر سياق الآية وكذا ما في سورة طه من آيات القصة أن موسى غضب على هارون كما غضب على بني إسرائيل

TABATABAI:7:150/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:150/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:150/r6.claim: Different temperaments and practical judgments between two infallible prophets are possible: infallibility governs divine rulings, not dispositions or ways of life.
TABATABAI:7:150/r6.anchor: وهذا المقدار من الاختلاف في السليقة والمشيئة بين نبيين معصومين لا دليل على منعه

TABATABAI:7:150/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:150/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:150/r7.claim: Moses took Aaron's head as if preparing to strike him because he thought Aaron had acted independently; this was discipline over advisory judgment, not punishment for violating a binding command, and Aaron was right.
TABATABAI:7:150/r7.anchor: فما وقع منه إنما هو تأديب في أمر إرشادي لا عقاب في أمر مولوي وإن كان الحق في ذلك مع هارون

TABATABAI:7:150/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:150/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:150/r8.claim: An alternative says Moses handled Aaron as people handle themselves in anger, gripping a beard or biting a lip, because he regarded his brother as himself.
TABATABAI:7:150/r8.anchor: أن موسى إنما فعل ذلك مستعظما لفعلهم مفكرا فيما كان منهم كما يفعل الإنسان ذلك بنفسه

TABATABAI:7:150/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:150/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:150/r9.claim: Another alternative says Moses displayed his anger at the Israelites' apostasy to show its gravity and deter future conduct.
TABATABAI:7:150/r9.anchor: أنه أراد أن يظهر ما اعتراه من الغضب على قومه لإكباره منهم ما صاروا وإليه من الكفر والارتداد

TABATABAI:7:150/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:150/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:150/r10.claim: Another explanation says Moses pulled Aaron close to consult him privately and ask what had happened.
TABATABAI:7:150/r10.anchor: أنه إنما جره إلى نفسه ليناجيه ويستفسر حال القوم منه

TABATABAI:7:150/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:150/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:150/r11.claim: A fourth explanation says Moses took Aaron's head compassionately because Aaron shared his grief, while Aaron feared people would mistake the gesture for insult.
TABATABAI:7:150/r11.anchor: أنه لما رأى أن بهارون مثل ما به من الغضب والأسف أخذ برأسه متوجعا له

TABATABAI:7:150/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:150/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:150/r12.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says most or all of these alternative explanations do not fit the passage's context.
TABATABAI:7:150/r12.anchor: وجل هذه الوجوه أو كلها لا تلائم سياق الآيات

TABATABAI:7:150/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:150/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:150/r13.claim: The opening says Moses already knew of the people's apostasy before seeing them, because God told him at the appointment, as Ta-Ha recounts.
TABATABAI:7:150/r13.anchor: وقوله في صدر الآية { ولما رجع موسى إلى قومه غضبان أسفا } يدل على أنه كان عالما بأمر ارتداد قومه من قبل

TABATABAI:7:151-153/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:151-153/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:151-153/r1.claim: Although Moses knew of the apostasy, anger manifested when he saw the people: knowledge produces grief, while witnessing the offender enables defensive or retaliatory action; seeing an event alone differs from seeing it with others.
TABATABAI:7:151-153/r1.anchor: لأن للعلم حكما وللمشاهدة حكما آخر، والغضب هيجان القوة الدافعة للدفع أو الانتقام

TABATABAI:7:152/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:152/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:7:152/r3.claim: The Prophet says God have mercy on Moses: after hearing that his people had been tested he did not throw the tablets, but seeing them himself, he threw them and some broke; seeing is not like hearing.
TABATABAI:7:152/r3.anchor: ليس المعاين كالمخبر أخبره ربه تبارك وتعالى أن قومه فتنوا بعده فلم يلق الألواح

TABATABAI:7:152/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:152/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:7:152/r4.claim: Al-Ṣādiq reports that merely hearing from God that the people had made a calf did not affect Moses as seeing them did; once he saw them, his anger intensified and he cast the tablets.
TABATABAI:7:152/r4.anchor: لما أخبر موسى أن قومه اتخذوا عجلا

TABATABAI:7:152/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:152/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:7:152/r5.claim: Al-Ṣādiq adds that direct seeing has an advantage over receiving a report.
TABATABAI:7:152/r5.anchor: قد قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام وللرؤية فضل على الخبر

TABATABAI:7:152/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:152/r6.speaker: علي كرم الله وجهه
TABATABAI:7:152/r6.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAlī renders the word as “juʾār,” with an initial ḍamma and hamza, meaning a loud sound.
TABATABAI:7:152/r6.anchor: وعن علي كرم الله وجهه أنه قرأ " جؤار " بجيم مضمومة وهمزة

TABATABAI:7:152/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:152/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:152/r7.claim: Reports say the tablets were made of emerald or the lote tree of Paradise, were twelve cubits long, were written while Moses heard the pens, or were preserved inside a mountain or stone in Yemen; the author regards these as unsupported isolated reports unnecessary to exegesis.
TABATABAI:7:152/r7.anchor: وكذا ما ورد من طرق الشيعة وأهل السنة أن ألواح التوراة كانت من زبرجد

ZAJJAJ:v2p378/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p378/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p378/r3.claim: Ghaḍbāna is an accusative circumstantial, on the faʿlān pattern with feminine faʿlā, and is diptote because of its alif and nūn, like ḥamrāʾ.
ZAJJAJ:v2p378/r3.anchor: منصوب على الحال، وهو على مثال فعلان، وله فعلى نحو غضبى

ZAJJAJ:v2p378/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p378/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p378/r4.claim: Asaf means intense anger; 43:55 uses āsafūnā to mean they angered Us.
ZAJJAJ:v2p378/r4.anchor: الشديد الغضب، قال الله جل وعز: (فلما آسفونا انتقمنا منهم)

ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r1.claim: ʿAjila al-amra means to get ahead of or precede an affair, while aʿjala means to urge it on.
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r1.anchor: يقال عجلت الأمر والشيء سبقته، وأعجلته استحثثته

ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r2.claim: The vocative is read ibn umm with fatḥa or ibn umm with kasra.
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r2.anchor: بالفتح وإن شئت بن أم بالكسر

ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r3.claim: The fatḥa reflects frequent use of ibn umm and ibn ʿamm; in vocative speech the two words are treated as one compound, like fifteen.
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r3.anchor: فجعلوا " ابن " و " أم " شيئا واحدا نحو خمسة عشر

ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r4.claim: With kasra, the phrase is annexed to the speaker after first being treated as a single name.
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r4.anchor: فإنه أضافه إلى نفسه بعد أن جعله اسما واحدا

ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r5.speaker: العرب
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r5.claim: Some Arabs retain the yāʾ and say yā ibn ummī.
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r5.anchor: يقول: يا ابن أمي بإثبات الياء

ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r6.claim: Zajjaj cites the unnamed poet's line as evidence for the yā ibn ummī vocative.
ZAJJAJ:v2p378#2/r6.anchor: يا ابن أمي ويا شسقيق نفسي. . .

TABRISI:7:150-151/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:150-151/r1.speaker: ابن عامر وأهل الكوفة عن عاصم
TABRISI:7:150-151/r1.claim: They read ibn um with kasra here and in Ṭā Hā; the other readers put ibn um in the accusative in both places.
TABRISI:7:150-151/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأهل الكوفة عن عاصم ابن أم بالكسر ههنا وفي طه

TABRISI:7:150-151/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:150-151/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:7:150-151/r2.claim: In a noncanonical reading, Mujāhid has tašmit with fatḥa on tāʾ and mīm and al-aʿdāʾ in the accusative; he also reports yashmit with yāʾ.
